title: Automorphic congruences and reverse main-conjecture divisibilities
summary: Target-level plan of AutomorphicCongruences part L0 (stages L0, L1, L2, L2s, L3, L4, L5, L5a; L5b and L5w are the accepted part AutomorphicCongruences--L5b). L0 plans the Σ-primitive Selmer instances, the primitive/imprimitive and specialization comparisons, the Eisenstein ideal, Skinner–Urban's polarized lattice datum and lattice construction with its local conditions, the canonical-period congruence comparison and the exact CM-theta integrality input. L1 plans Skinner–Urban's GU(2,2) argument (ordinary Hermitian forms and Hida theory, the Eisenstein datum, Klingen Eisenstein series by pullback, the three-variable p-adic L-function, the Eisenstein family, coefficient coprimality, the pseudo-character, the Selmer lower bound and Theorems 3.6.1 and Corollary 3.6.3). L2s plans Castella–Liu–Wan's semi-ordinary GU(3,1) theory and divisibility (Thm 8.2.1 (1) and (2)); L2 plans Fouquet–Wan's general-weight GU(3,1) divisibility (Thm 7.32), Wan's ordinary Rankin–Selberg divisibility, the Kings–Loeffler–Zerbes Beilinson–Flach classes and reciprocity, the Castella–Wan equivalence, the crystalline theorem 4.51 and the §4.8 ordinary reverse divisibility (Thm 1.6). L3 plans Fouquet–Wan's deformation-ring facts, fundamental lines and Nakamura's universal zeta morphism with its specialization to Kato's; L4 plans the descent to the universal-family and pointwise theorems (Thms 5.2, 5.1) and Nakamura's §5 consequences; L5 is an aggregate; L5a plans Burungale–Castella–Skinner's early product divisibility (Prop. 5.2.1) with the ordinary two-variable equivalence (Thm 4.1.3) as an interface to the planned KatoEulerSystems L5 owner. All eight stages are planned; seventeen gaps and twenty requests are recorded; the RS-11 ownership (with its review pending) and the thirteen confirmed red-team findings are followed. Independent review corrected the source contracts and supplier scope, including the later CLW two-family repair. This is a complete review pass with target-planned stages and explicit gaps, not a gap-free or formalized roadmap.

nodes.title: Σ-primitive ordinary Selmer groups over Iwasawa towers
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, A a profinite ℤ_p-algebra, T a free A-module of finite rank with a continuous A-linear G_F-action, and for each place v | p a G_{F_v}-stable A-direct summand T_v ⊆ T with T/T_v free. For a finite set Σ of finite places, Sel^Σ_F(T,(T_v)) is the kernel of the restriction from H¹(F, T ⊗_A A^∨) (A^∨ the Pontryagin dual) to the product over v ∉ Σ, v ∤ p of H¹(I_v, T ⊗ A^∨) and over v | p of H¹(I_v, (T/T_v) ⊗ A^∨): no condition at Σ away from p, unramified elsewhere away from p, and the ordinary (Greenberg) condition at p. Its dual X^Σ_F = Hom_A(Sel^Σ_F, A^∨) is finitely generated over A. For an extension E/F inside a ℤ_p^d-tower, Sel^Σ_E is the direct limit over finite subextensions and X^Σ_E the inverse limit, and Shapiro's lemma identifies Sel^Σ_{F_∞}(T) with Sel^Σ_F(T ⊗_A Λ_{F,A}(ε_F^{-1})) as Λ_{F,A}-modules, where Λ_{F,A} = A ⊗̂ ℤ_p[[Gal(F_∞/F)]] and ε_F is the tautological character. When A is noetherian and normal, Ch^Σ_{F,A}(T) denotes the characteristic ideal of X^Σ_F(T) and Ft^Σ_{F,A}(T) its Fitting ideal. The p-condition is imposed for every v|p regardless of membership in Σ. For torsion X, Ch means the divisorial ideal of its length divisor; noetherian normal does not imply principal. Use SU’s zero characteristic-ideal convention if X is not torsion.
hypotheses: T free of finite rank over the profinite ℤ_p-algebra A, with a continuous action of G_F; T_v free direct summands with free quotients for v | p.
Σ is finite. If S contains Σ, p and the ramification of T, the same kernel may be computed using H¹(G_{F,S},−); membership of p in Σ does not remove its local condition.
The characteristic ideal is used only over noetherian normal A, as the divisorial ideal of height-one lengths.
proofSteps: Instantiate the imported Selmer kernel with relaxed conditions at Σ away from p, unramified conditions at other non-p places, and Greenberg conditions from T_v at all v|p.
Finite generation of the dual: H¹(G_{F,S}, M ⊗ A^∨) is cofinitely generated for finitely generated M (SU Lemma 3.1.9, after Greenberg).
Shapiro: the coinduced module of A^∨ along Gal(F_n/F) has direct limit Λ_{F,A}^∨(ε_F^{-1}); the restriction maps at v correspond to the products over places of F_n above v (SU 3.1.2, Prop. 3.2.3).
Define Ch^Σ via the height-one length divisor of X^Σ and Ft^Σ via Fitting ideals of a presentation.
acceptance: If T_v=T at all p-places and S contains Σ, p and ram(T), then Sel^Σ_F=H¹(G_{F,S},T⊗A^∨) when S=Σ∪{v|p}∪ram(T) and ram(T) away from p lies in Σ.
For Σ⊂Σ′ the quotient embeds in the sum of changed local-condition quotients; surjectivity onto all local terms needs the additional hypotheses of primitive-imprimitive-comparison.

nodes.title: Primitive against Σ-primitive Selmer groups and the removed Euler factors
nodes.statement: Let T, (T_v) and A be as in L0/sigma-primitive-selmer with A noetherian normal, F any number field, and S a finite set of finite places not above p at which T is unramified, contained in Σ. Then (i) Ch^Σ_{F,A}(T) ⊇ Ch^{Σ∖S}_{F,A}(T) · ∏_{v∈S} det_A(1 − q_v^{-1} frob_v^{-1} | T) (SU Lemma 3.2.15, Cor. 3.2.16); (ii) over ℚ_∞, the Pontryagin dual of H¹_Σ(ℚ_∞, T ⊗ A^∨) = ∏_{v∈Σ, v∤p} H¹(ℚ_{∞,v}, T ⊗ A^∨) is a finitely generated torsion Λ_{ℚ,A}-module with no nonzero pseudo-null submodule, and its characteristic ideal is generated by ∏_{ℓ∈Σ} P_{T,ℓ}(ℓ^{-1} ε_ℚ(frob_ℓ)), P_{T,ℓ}(X) = det(1 − X frob_ℓ^{-1} | (T⊗_A Frac A)^{I_ℓ}) (SU Lemma 3.2.17); (iii) when the primitive dual is torsion and the global-to-local map is surjective (Greenberg–Vatsal), Ch^Σ = Ch^∅ · ∏_{ℓ∈Σ} P_{T,ℓ}(ℓ^{-1}ε(frob_ℓ)) (SU Prop. 3.2.18). On the analytic side the Σ-imprimitive p-adic L-functions are defined by multiplying the primitive ones by the same Euler-factor elements, so every removed factor is matched by the identical element of Λ.
hypotheses: For (i), A is noetherian normal and T is unramified at S, a finite set away from p. For the local cyclotomic module in (ii), use the compact finite-type coefficients of SU §3.2.2; the characteristic-divisor assertion also requires normal noetherian A.

For the exact sequence in (iii), A admits decreasing ideals I_n with intersection zero and each A/I_n finite free over Z_p; the primitive X_Q∞(T,T_p) is Λ_Q,A-torsion; T* (the Pontryagin dual in SU §3.1.3) has no nonzero A-submodule with trivial G_Q action; Σ∪{p} contains ram(T). For every finite Σ′⊂Σ, localization onto H¹_{Σ\Σ′} is then surjective (SU Prop. 3.2.18).

The Euler polynomial of Lemma 3.2.17 uses inverse frob_ℓ on rational inertia invariants. A rank-one invariant space gives 1−αX, where α is the eigenvalue of that precise inverse Frobenius. Integral lattices and analytic conventions must be compared explicitly.
proofSteps: (i): the cokernel of Sel^{Σ∖S} → Sel^Σ injects into ∏_{v∈S} H¹(I_v, T ⊗ A^∨)^{G_{F_v}}, whose dual has characteristic ideal det(1 − q_v^{-1}frob_v^{-1}|T) because T is unramified at v.
(ii): Shapiro over ℚ_∞ and local Tate duality compute the local terms; each is Λ-torsion with characteristic ideal the displayed Euler factor, and has no pseudo-null submodule.
(iii): with the localization map surjective the sequence 0 → Sel^∅ → Sel^Σ → H¹_Σ → 0 is exact, and multiplicativity of characteristic ideals gives equality.

Analytic matching: the Σ-imprimitive p-adic L-function is by definition the primitive one times ∏_{ℓ∈Σ} P_ℓ(ℓ^{-1}γ_ℓ), so the comparison of characteristic ideals and of analytic functions involves the same elements.
acceptance: Transfer a primitive/imprimitive bound only after matching identical Euler elements on the arithmetic and analytic sides; do not cancel a vanishing specialization.

A Steinberg Euler element is a unit in the local power-series ring exactly when its residue at augmentation is nonzero. With ℓ=11, p=5 and α=1, 1−ℓ^{-1}γ has augmentation 10/11, so it is not a unit even though the residual representation can be ramified.

nodes.statement: Let F_∞ be ℚ_∞, K_∞ or K^+_∞, A a profinite ℤ_p-algebra, 𝔞 ⊂ A an ideal and T as in L0/sigma-primitive-selmer. Assume the explicit SU Prop. 3.2.8 hypotheses below, so that X^Σ_{F_∞}(T)/𝔞 ≅ X^Σ_{F_∞}(T/𝔞T). Then (i) Ft^Σ_{F,A/𝔞}(T/𝔞T) = Ft^Σ_{F,A}(T) mod 𝔞; (ii) if A and A/𝔞 are noetherian normal domains and (f) ⊇ Ch^Σ_{F,A}(T) is principal, then f mod 𝔞 divides Ch^Σ_{F,A/𝔞}(T/𝔞T); in particular when A is factorial Ch^Σ_{F,A}(T) mod 𝔞 divides Ch^Σ_{F,A/𝔞}(T/𝔞T). (iii) For the descent K_∞ → K^+_∞ along I^- = ker(Λ_K → Λ_ℚ), X^Σ_{K_∞}(T)/I^- ≅ X^Σ_{K^+_∞}(T), and when A is factorial Ch^Σ_{K_∞}(T) mod I^- divides Ch^Σ_{K^+_∞}(T).
hypotheses: In SU Prop. 3.2.8, inertia at p acts on T/T_p through Γ_Q; Σ∪{p} contains ram(T); F∞ is Q∞, K∞ or K⁺∞; T* (the Pontryagin dual in SU §3.1.3) has no nonzero A-subquotient on which G_F acts trivially. These hypotheses apply for every ideal 𝔞 under consideration, not merely a presumed control isomorphism.

The control isomorphism for a general ideal 𝔞 of the coefficient ring is SU Prop. 3.2.8 and is owned here; the upstream derived control (SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3) covers the specialization to finite layers of a one-variable tower and is used only there. The control isomorphism needs SU Prop. 3.2.8's hypotheses; without them only a map with kernel and cokernel controlled by H⁰ and local terms exists.
Characteristic ideals do not commute with base change in general; only the principal majorant transfers (ii). A specialization at which f vanishes gives no information.

The characteristic ideal is the smallest divisorial ideal containing the Fitting ideal; a principal ideal is divisorial, so (f) ⊇ Ch ⊇ Ft and reduction gives f mod 𝔞 ∣ Ft(T/𝔞) ⊆ Ch(T/𝔞) (ii).
For (iii), Shapiro along Γ^-_K and Prop. 3.2.8 identify Sel^Σ_{K^+_∞} with the I^- torsion of Sel^Σ_{K_∞}, and (ii) applies.

nodes.title: The Eisenstein ideal of an Eisenstein family
nodes.statement: Let Λ be a noetherian complete local domain, 𝕋 a reduced finite Λ-algebra generated over Λ by the images of a set 𝒯 of Hecke operators acting on a space of Λ-adic cusp forms, and λ: 𝒯 → Λ the system of eigenvalues of a Λ-adic Eisenstein family E (a Λ-algebra homomorphism from the abstract Hecke algebra). The Eisenstein ideal I_E ⊆ 𝕋 is the ideal generated by t − λ(t) for t ∈ 𝒯; when the structure map Λ → 𝕋/I_E is surjective, the Eisenstein ideal of Λ is its kernel E_E, so that Λ/E_E ≅ 𝕋/I_E. When I_E is proper, 𝕋_E denotes the localization of 𝕋 at the maximal ideal containing I_E.
hypotheses: 𝕋 is generated over Λ by 𝒯 together with the U_p-operators, so Λ → 𝕋/I_E is surjective; otherwise E_E is defined as the kernel on the image.
The Hecke operators are those at primes outside a fixed finite set Σ, the U_p-operators, and the central or diamond operators used by the source.
proofSteps: Define I_E as the ideal generated by {t − λ(t) : t ∈ 𝒯} and E_E := ker(Λ → 𝕋/I_E).
Surjectivity follows because the generators of 𝕋 over Λ act by scalars of Λ modulo I_E.
acceptance: The congruence statements of L1, L2 and L2s are lower bounds ord_P(E_E) ≥ ord_P(L) for height-one primes P of Λ, from a cuspidal family congruent to E.

nodes.title: The Skinner–Urban lattice datum
nodes.statement: Let H = G ⋊ {1, c} with c of order two, A a complete discrete valuation ring with fraction field F and maximal ideal m, and R a local reduced finite flat A-algebra with R/M = A/m. A lattice datum consists of: (1) a character ν: H → A^×; (2) a character χ: G → A^× with χ̄ ≠ ν̄χ̄^{-c}, and χ′ := νχ^{-c}; (3) a representation ρ: G → Aut_A(V), V ≅ A^n, with ρ^c ≅ ρ^∨ ⊗ ν, ρ̄ absolutely irreducible and ρ residually disjoint from χ and χ′ (some x ∈ A[G] has coprime residual characteristic polynomials); (4) a representation σ: G → Aut_{R⊗F}(M), M ≅ (R ⊗ F)^{n+2}, with σ^c ≅ σ^∨ ⊗ ν, tr σ(G) ⊆ R and finitely generated R[G]-orbits; (5) a proper ideal I ⊂ R with J := A ∩ I ≠ 0, A/J ≅ R/I and tr σ ≡ χ′ + tr ρ + χ mod I. Local data at a subgroup D ⊂ G: a D-stable free summand M^+ ⊆ M with free quotient, a D-stable free summand V^+ ⊆ V, and the congruence Ch(M^+, x, T) ≡ Ch(V^+, x, T)(1 − Tχ(x)) mod I for x ∈ R[D]. The datum is ν-polarized when ν is compatible (Φ^t = −ν(c)Φ) with the polarization of ρ.
hypotheses: The polarization conditions are those of SU 4.2.2; residual disjointness is in the sense of SU 4.1.2.

In applications G = G_{K,Σ}, H = G_{ℚ,Σ}, D a decomposition group at a prime above p, A the completion of a localization of a two-variable Iwasawa algebra at a height-one prime P, and R a completed local Hecke algebra.

SU §4.3 requires the common residue field κ to have at least n+2 nonzero elements. To deduce compatibility of ν with σ from Lemma 4.3.3, require char κ≠2 and absolute irreducibility of every field factor σ_i; otherwise compatibility with σ is a separate hypothesis of the Selmer consequence.
SU Ch(θ,x,T)=det(1−Tθ(x)); convert Mathlib’s det(TI−θ(x)) before invoking polynomial congruences.
proofSteps: Record the data (1)–(5) and the local data 4.5.1–4.5.3 as fields; derive the congruence for the quotients M^- and V^- from 4.3.1.
Residual disjointness gives projectors x_1, x_2 ∈ B[G] with x_i acting as identity on one summand and zero on the other (SU Lemma 4.1.3, via the Henselian property).
acceptance: The SU instance (SU 7.3.2), the CLW instance (proof of CLW Thm 8.2.1, items (1)–(5)) and the FW instance (proof of FW Thm 7.32) are all lattice data with n = 2.

nodes.title: The lattice construction: Eisenstein ideals bound Selmer groups
nodes.statement: Let (ν, χ, ρ, σ, I) be a ν-polarized lattice datum (L0/su-lattice-datum) with H = G_{ℚ,Σ}, G = G_{K,Σ}, local data at D = G_{K,p} satisfying SU 4.5.1–4.5.3, with V^+_0 ⊕ A(χ) and V^-_0 ⊕ A(χ′) residually disjoint modulo P, where A = Â_{0,P} for a height-one prime P of a noetherian normal domain A_0, and J = A ∩ I. Then (i) ord_P Ch^Σ_ℚ(ψν) ≥ ℓ_P(L(χ′)/J(χ′)); (ii) ord_P Ch^Σ_K(ρ_0 ⊗ χ^{-1}) ≥ ℓ_P(N/N′), and in particular ord_P Ch^Σ_K(ρ_0 ⊗ χ^{-1}) ≥ ord_P(J) when N′ = 0 (SU Prop. 4.5.6); (iii) if ord_P Ch^Σ_ℚ(ψν) = 0 then ord_P Ch^Σ_K(ρ_0 ⊗ χ^{-1}) ≥ ord_P(J) (SU Cor. 4.5.7); (iv) under SU Lemma 4.3.11, if ord_P(J) > ord_P Ch^Σ_ℚ(ψν) then ord_P Ch^Σ_K(ρ_0 ⊗ χ^{-1}) ≥ 1 (SU Prop. 4.5.8). Here the Selmer groups are the Σ-primitive ones of L0/sigma-primitive-selmer for the pairs (A_0(ψν), 0) and (V_0(χ^{-1}), V^+_0(χ^{-1})). The variant of Wan20 Prop. 9.2 replaces the irreducibility of σ by condition (9): every specialization σ_λ is absolutely irreducible or contains an absolutely irreducible two-dimensional subrepresentation with trace ≡ χ + χ′ modulo I.
hypotheses: P is a height-one prime of A_0 with A_0 noetherian normal; the polarization ν is compatible with the polarization of ρ (4.5.5.a).
The bound concerns the Σ-primitive groups; primitive versions follow by L0/primitive-imprimitive-comparison.
The excluded case ord_P Ch^Σ_ℚ(ψν) > 0 is where the abelian Selmer group may absorb the extensions; CLW and Wan exclude such P explicitly.

Use SU §4.4 descent: A_0 is a profinite Krull domain with height-one P and completion A; R_0 is a reduced local finite A_0-algebra with Q over P and completed R; ρ descends to the free A_0-representation V_0, σ has trace in R_0 and finite R_0[G]-orbits, and I_0,J_0 are the contractions. G,H are profinite and representations continuous.

For SU §4.5.5 require ν compatible with the polarization Φ of σ, and V⁺_0 an A_0-free direct summand stable under G_Qp. This compatibility follows from Lemma 4.3.3 only in odd residue characteristic with each σ_i absolutely irreducible.

The Wan20 Prop. 9.2 variant requires all its setup (1)–(9), including a rank-one local M⁺ character congruence and disjoint M⁻ constituent. Its condition (9) permits a two-dimensional absolutely irreducible subrepresentation whose trace is congruent to χ+χ′, not χ+χ^{-c} unless ν=1. The auxiliary one-dimensional Selmer factor must have valuation zero for the full length-of-J bound.
proofSteps: Choose a lattice ℒ ⊂ M stable under R[G]; the residual projectors of the datum decompose ℒ into pieces ℒ(χ′), ℒ(ρ), ℒ(χ) with submodules 𝒥(·) cut out by I (SU 4.3, Cor. 4.3.9).

Off-diagonal blocks define cocycles: φ ↦ c_φ(g) = (φ ⊗ id)(χ^{-1}(g)σ(g)ε̄* − ε̄*) gives Hom_{A_0}(N, A_0^∨) → H¹(G, V_0 ⊗ A_0^∨(χ^{-1})), whose dual is surjective after localizing at P (SU Props 4.4.4–4.4.5).

Local conditions: the projector x^+ ∈ R[D] splits the D-extension, so a multiple t ∉ P of the image lies in the kernel of restriction to H¹(D, V^-_0 ⊗ A_0^∨(χ^{-1})), i.e. satisfies the ordinary condition (SU Prop. 4.5.4); by polarization the same holds at the conjugate prime.
Lengths: the dual Selmer group surjects onto Hom(N, A_0^∨)^∨ localized at P, giving (ii); (iii) and (iv) follow from (i), Lemma 4.3.8 and Lemma 4.3.11.

For Wan20 Prop. 9.2 read and verify setup (1)–(9), retaining its rank-one ordinary line and alternative two-dimensional irreducible-subrepresentation case. This source-specific polarized construction is not a specialization of the supplier’s two-dimensional local Ribet theorem.
acceptance: A height-one prime with ord_P(J) = 2 and N′ = 0 must give ord_P(Ch) ≥ 2, not just ≥ 1.
Excluded-prime check: when ord_P Ch^Σ_ℚ(ψν) > 0 and Lemma 4.3.11 fails, no conclusion is drawn.
The extension classes are those of the automorphic family; the theorem does not presuppose any divisibility of characteristic ideals.

nodes.statement: In the situation of L0/lattice-construction, the classes [c_φ] obtained from the off-diagonal blocks of σ satisfy, after multiplication by an element t ∉ P: (a) at every place v ∉ Σ they are unramified, since σ is unramified outside Σ; (b) at the primes above p they lie in the kernel of restriction to H¹(D, V^-_0 ⊗ A_0^∨(χ^{-1})) for D = G_{K,p} (the ordinary condition), and by the polarization the corresponding statement holds at G_{K,p̄}; (c) at places v ∈ Σ, v ∤ p, no condition is imposed (Σ-primitive). (b) is SU Prop. 4.5.4(ii): the projector x^+ acts as identity on M^+ and kills M^-, so the extension restricted to D splits along the filtration.

nodes.title: Ordinary p-adic Hermitian modular forms on GU(2,2) and their Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: Let K be an imaginary quadratic field in which p splits, G = G_2 = GU(2,2) the unitary similitude group of the skew-Hermitian form w_2 = (0 1_2; −1_2 0) over O_K, and K′ ⊂ G(𝔸^p_f) a neat open compact subgroup. On the ordinary locus of the integral model of the Shimura variety S_G(K′K_p) (with its toroidal and minimal compactifications), and over its Igusa tower, define the space V^q_{a,ord} (dual of the ordinary p-adic Hermitian modular forms; q = 0 for cusp forms, q = 1 for all forms) of weight a with coefficients in Λ_2 = ℤ_p[[Γ_2]], Γ_2 = (1 + pℤ_p)^4 ⊂ T_2(ℤ_p), with the q-expansions at the cusps x = diag(u, t ū^{-1}), the Hecke operators at unramified places, the U_p-operators u_t for t = diag(p^{a_1},…,p^{a_4}), the ordinary projector e = lim u_t^{n!}, and the universal ordinary cuspidal Hecke algebra h_{Σ,0}(K′; Λ). Specializations at arithmetic weights are classical holomorphic Hermitian modular forms of weight (κ, κ; 0, 0)-type when the weight is sufficiently regular. Write M^q=Hom_Λ(V^q,Λ) for the module of forms carrying q-expansions: V and M are dual carriers and are not identified without a pairing.
hypotheses: p splits in K; K′K_p neat; the p-adic weights are characters of T_2(ℤ_p) through Γ_2 and µ_{p−1}^4.

nodes.title: Hida theory for GU(2,2): freeness, control and the boundary sequence
nodes.statement: For n = 2 and q = 0 (cusp forms) or q = 1 (all forms): (i) V^q_{a,ord} is free of finite rank over Λ_n, and its specializations at finite-order characters ψ of level s have rank independent of ψ and of the weight (SU Thm 6.3.3); (ii) for any Λ_n-algebra A there is a short exact sequence 0 → M^0_{a,ord}(K^p, A) → M^1_{a,ord}(K^p, A) →Φ ⊕_{[g] ∈ C_{n−1}(K)} M^0_{a′,ord}(K^p_{n−1,g}, Λ_{n−1}) ⊗ A → 0, Φ the sum of the Siegel operators to the boundary components (cusp forms on G_{n−1} = GU(1,1)) (SU Thm 6.3.10, from Cor. 5.5.9); (iii) for every sufficiently regular algebraic dominant weight k the canonical surjection h^{S,q}(K^p; Λ_n) ⊗ Λ_n/P_k ↠ h^{S,q}_{k,ord}(K) has nilpotent kernel, so every ℚ̄_p-valued character of the Λ-adic Hecke algebra at P_k comes from a classical ordinary eigenform of weight k (SU Thm 6.4.1). Consequently h_{Σ,0}(K′; Λ) is finite over Λ_2 and its arithmetic points of regular weight are Zariski dense.
hypotheses: Weights sufficiently regular in the sense of SU 6.2; neat level; p split in K.
proofSteps: Freeness from vertical control on the Igusa tower (SU §6.2–6.3, Props 6.2.5, Cor. 6.2.6, Thm 6.2.10).
Boundary exact sequence: the Siegel operator surjects onto boundary ordinary forms (SU Cor. 5.5.9, Thm 6.3.10).
Control of the Hecke algebra in sufficiently regular weight (nilpotent kernel, SU Thm 6.4.1); density of such weights in Spec Λ_2.
acceptance: The boundary sequence is what lets one subtract an Eisenstein family from a lift and obtain a cusp form congruent to it.

nodes.title: The p-adic Eisenstein datum and its Eisenstein ideal
nodes.statement: A p-adic Eisenstein datum D = (A, 𝕀, 𝐟, ψ, ξ, Σ) consists of the ring of integers A of a finite extension of ℚ_p containing ℤ[µ_{M_D p}, i, D_K^{1/2}], a normal domain 𝕀 finite over Λ_{W,A}, an 𝕀-adic ordinary eigenform 𝐟 of tame level M, finite idele class characters ψ and ξ of 𝔸_K^× (ψ|_{𝔸^×} = χ_𝐟), and a finite set of primes Σ containing those dividing M p D_K and the ramification of ξ. Put Λ_D = 𝕀[[Γ^-_K × Γ_K]], a finite local reduced Λ_2-algebra via α ⊗ β (SU 6.5.1), the characters σ_ψ, σ_ξ, σ_{ξ′} = σ_ξσ^c_ξ, and the semisimple representation ρ_D = σ_{χ̄_f,0}σ^c_ψε^{-3} ⊕ (ρ_𝐟 ⊗ σ_{χ̄_f,0}σ^{-c}_ξσ^c_ψε^{-2}) ⊕ σ_{χ̄_f,0}ε^{-1}det ρ_𝐟 σ^{-1}_{ξ′}σ^c_ψ of G_K over Frac Λ_D (6.5.2.a). The Eisenstein ideal I_D ⊆ h_D = h_{Σ,0}(K′; Λ_D) is generated by the coefficients of Q_v(X) − Q_{v,D}(X) (v ∉ Σ), the relations u_t − ∏β_i^{a_i} for the U_p-operators with the prescribed (β_1,…,β_4), and the central operators Z_{ℓ,0}, Z^{(i)}_{ℓ,0} minus their values on the Eisenstein characters; 𝔈_D ⊆ Λ_D is the kernel of Λ_D → h_D/I_D, so Λ_D/𝔈_D ≅ h_D/I_D (6.5.3.a), and 𝕋_D is the localization of h_D at the maximal ideal containing I_D. The two p-adic L-functions attached to D are L^Σ_{𝐟,K,ξ} ∈ 𝕀[[Γ_K]] (L1/su-padic-l-function) and L^Σ_{χ̄_𝐟ξ̄′}, the image of the Kubota–Leopoldt function of the Dirichlet character χ̄_𝐟ξ̄′; their product is L_D.
hypotheses: ψ exists with ψ|_{𝔸^×} = χ_𝐟 and unramified outside Σ (SU Thm 12.3.1 hypothesis); (irred)_𝐟 and (dist)_𝐟 when 𝕋_D is used.
proofSteps: Define Λ_D, the characters and ρ_D as in SU 6.5.1–6.5.2.
Instantiate L0/eisenstein-ideal with the Hecke operators listed in SU 6.5.3 and the eigensystem of ρ_D and the U_p-characters.
acceptance: The specialization of ρ_D at an arithmetic point with an associated Eisenstein series is the Galois representation of that Eisenstein series (SU remark after (6.5.2.a)).

nodes.title: Klingen Eisenstein series on GU(2,2) as pullbacks of Siegel Eisenstein series on GU(3,3)
nodes.statement: For a cuspidal eigenform f on GU(1,1) (from an elliptic newform and a character ψ), a character ξ of 𝔸_K^× and a choice of local sections at the places of Σ and at p, construct the holomorphic Klingen-type Eisenstein series E(Z, x; F) on GU(2,2), induced from the Klingen parabolic with Levi GU(1,1) × Res_{K/ℚ}𝔾_m, of weight κ > 6 (SU §9, 'good Eisenstein series' Prop. 9.3.3), its Hecke eigenvalues and Satake parameters (SU §9.5–9.6), and its expression through the pullback of a Siegel Eisenstein series on GU(3,3) along GU(2,2) × GU(1,1) ↪ GU(3,3) paired against f (SU §11, Prop. 11.2.3). The local sections at p and at Σ are chosen as in SU §11.4, so that the Fourier coefficients c(β, x) are products of local Whittaker integrals with explicit values (SU Cor. 11.7.5–11.7.6, §11.8), the singular ones (det β = 0) being multiples of the L-values L^Σ_K(f, χ̄_fξ, κ − 1)·L^Σ(χ̄_fξ̄′, κ − 2).
hypotheses: κ > 6 for the absolutely convergent range; the sections at p have conductor dividing p as in (12.4.2.a) when the family is formed.
The doubling/pullback formalism, the Siegel Eisenstein series on unitary groups and the local doubling integrals are imported; this node owns the Klingen-specific choices and coefficient formulas.
proofSteps: Pullback (doubling) formula: restricting E^{Sieg}_{GU(3,3)} to GU(2,2) × GU(1,1) and integrating against f gives the Klingen series times the standard L-value (SU Prop. 11.2.3, from Shimura/Garrett).
Local computations at unramified places, at Σ and at p (SU §11.4, Props 11.4.13, 11.4.17, 11.4.18, 11.4.23) and the Fourier coefficients (SU §11.6–11.7).
Hecke eigenvalues: E is an eigenform with Hecke polynomial Q_{v,D} (SU §9.5–9.6).
acceptance: The constant terms (Siegel operator images) and all singular Fourier coefficients are divisible by the product of the two L-values; the nonsingular ones are not in general.

nodes.title: The Skinner–Urban three-variable p-adic L-function
nodes.statement: Let A, 𝕀, 𝐟, ξ and Σ be as in a p-adic Eisenstein datum, and suppose there is a finite A-valued idele class character ψ with ψ|_{𝔸^×} = χ_𝐟, unramified outside Σ. (i) There is L̃^Σ_{𝐟,K,ξ} ∈ Frac(𝕀) ⊗_𝕀 𝕀_K whose value at every φ ∈ X_{𝕀_K,A}(𝐟, ψ, ξ) is the Petersson-normalized algebraic part of L^Σ_K(f_φ, χ̄_{f_φ}ξ_φ, κ_φ − 1) (SU Thm 12.3.1(i)); (ii) under (irred)_𝐟 and (dist)_𝐟 there is L^Σ_{𝐟,K,ξ} ∈ 𝕀_K whose value at φ is u_{f_φ} times the same L-value normalized by the canonical periods Ω^+_{f_φ}Ω^-_{f_φ}, u_{f_φ} a p-adic unit (SU Thm 12.3.1(ii)). (iii) If moreover χ_𝐟 = 1, ξ = ξ̄^c with conductor dividing (p), (M, D_K) = 1, M = M^+M^- with M^- squarefree with an odd number of primes, all inert in K, and ρ̄_𝐟 ramified at every ℓ | M^-, then L^Σ_{𝐟,K,ξ} lies in no prime of 𝕀[[Γ_K]] of the form Q·𝕀[[Γ_K]] with Q a height-one prime of 𝕀[[Γ^+_K]] (SU Prop. 12.3.6, from Vatsal's µ = 0). Precisely, the common numerator at φ is a(p,f_φ)^{-ord_p Nm(f_{χ̄_f ξ_φ})}·((κ_φ−2)!)²·g(χ̄_f ξ_φ)·Nm(f_{ξ_φ}d)^{κ_φ−2}·L_K^Σ(f_φ,χ̄_f ξ_φ,κ_φ−1). In (i) divide it by (−2πi)^{2κ_φ−2}·2^{-3}(2i)^{κ_φ+1}S(f_φ)⟨f_φ,f_φ^c|W_{N_φ}⟩; in (ii) divide by (−2πi)^{2κ_φ−2}Ω^+_{f_φ}Ω^-_{f_φ} and multiply by u_{f_φ}.
hypotheses: As stated; the interpolation set X_{𝕀_K,A}(𝐟, ψ, ξ) is defined in SU §12.3 (conductor conditions at p).
A contains i, sqrt(D_K), and the local Gauss sums g(ξ_ℓ^c,a_ℓδ_K), g(χ̄_f,ℓ ξ_ℓ^c,b_ℓδ_K), g(χ_f,ℓ ξ̄′_ℓ) for ℓ∈Σ\{p}, with conductors as in Prop. 12.2.5.
In (iii), every prime of M⁺ splits in K; the stated inert conditions apply to M⁻.
proofSteps: Apply the interpolation lemma 12.2.7 to the family g = f^{(1)}_{D,1/M,1} of Prop. 12.2.5; Cor. 11.7.5 identifies the specializations (proof of SU Thm 12.3.1).
Density of X′_D and independence of φ|_{Γ^-_K} place L̃ in Frac(𝕀) ⊗ 𝕀_K; the integral version N_g of Lemma 12.2.7(ii) gives (ii) (L0/canonical-period-congruence-number).

(iii): expand in γ^- − 1; the anticyclotomic specialization at a weight-two point has µ = 0 by Vatsal (through AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3h/finis-divisibility), so some coefficient is a unit and the series lies in no prime pulled back from 𝕀[[Γ^+_K]].
acceptance: Integrality (ii) requires (irred) and (dist); without them only (i) holds.
The interpolation uses the canonical periods Ω^±; the anticyclotomic restriction is compared with Bertolini–Darmon's function only up to a unit (SU 3.6.14).

sources.match: The two interpolation statements and the non-divisibility by pulled-back height-one primes from Vatsal's theorem.

nodes.title: The Λ_D-adic Klingen Eisenstein family and its constant terms
nodes.statement: Let D be a p-adic Eisenstein datum with cond(ψ_p), cond(ξ_p) | p, (irred)_𝐟 and (dist)_𝐟, and K′ ⊆ K′_D with K′K_p neat. (i) There is ℰ_D ∈ M^{a,ord}(K′; Λ_D) whose specialization at every φ ∈ X″_D is u_φ·G_{D_φ}/(Ω^+_{f_φ}Ω^-_{f_φ}) with |u_φ|_p = 1, G_{D_φ} the classical Klingen Eisenstein series (SU Thm 12.4.2(i), Thm 12.4.1); (ii) for x with x_p ∈ Q(ℤ_p) and det β = 0, the β-Fourier coefficient c_D(β, x) lies in L^Σ_{𝐟,K,ξ}·L^Σ_{χ̄_𝐟ξ̄′}·Λ_D (Thm 12.4.2(ii)); (iii) The full ordinary Hecke algebra h_D^full acting on all forms has the Eisenstein eigencharacter λ_D^full:h_D^full→Λ_D. The cuspidal Hecke algebra h_D^cusp only acquires this eigensystem modulo 𝔈_D, through Λ_D/𝔈_D≅h_D^cusp/I_D. SU uses h_D for the full algebra on p. 204 and the cuspidal algebra in §6.5.3. Consequently, if P ⊂ Λ_D is a height-one prime with ℰ_D ≢ 0 modulo P, then ord_P(𝔈_D) ≥ ord_P(L_D) (SU Thm 6.5.4): subtracting a lift of ℰ_D's constant terms produces a cuspidal family congruent to ℰ_D modulo L_D. Here ℰ_D denotes the Eisenstein form and 𝔈_D the coefficient-ring ideal; a hypothesis that the form is nonzero modulo P concerns ℰ_D.
hypotheses: (irred)_𝐟, (dist)_𝐟; A satisfies the hypotheses of SU Prop. 12.2.5; conductor condition (12.4.2.a) at p.
The conclusion of Thm 6.5.4 is conditional on ℰ_D being nonzero modulo P; L1/nonsingular-coefficient-coprimality supplies this.
proofSteps: Interpolate each q-expansion coefficient by Lemma 12.2.7 applied to f^{(2)}_{D,β,x} (proof of SU Thm 12.4.1), using Cor. 11.7.6.
Assemble a Λ_D-adic ordinary form by the q-expansion principle and Hida theory (L1/gu22-hida-control).

Thm 6.5.4: if ord_P(L_D) = r and ℰ_D ≢ 0 mod P, the boundary exact sequence lets one subtract a Λ_D-adic lift of ℰ_D's boundary values times L_D^{-1}·(unit), producing a cusp form H ≡ ℰ_D mod P^r, whence 𝕋_D/I_D surjects onto Λ_D/(𝔈_D, P^r).
acceptance: The congruence is with the whole family ℰ_D, not with an individual Eisenstein series; an interpolation formula for ℰ_D alone does not give it.
Excluded case: if ℰ_D ≡ 0 mod P no bound is claimed.

nodes.title: A nonsingular Fourier coefficient is prime to the p-adic L-function
nodes.statement: Let A be the ring of integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p, 𝕀 a domain finite over Λ_{W,A}, 𝐟 ∈ M^{ord}(M, 1; 𝕀) an 𝕀-adic newform with (irred)_𝐟 and (dist)_𝐟, and Σ_0 ⊇ {ℓ | pMD_K}. There is a finite Σ ⊇ Σ_0 such that for D = (A, 𝕀, 𝐟, 1, 1, Σ) the set C_D of nonsingular coefficients c_D(β_i, x) of ℰ_D satisfies: (i) every height-one prime of Λ_D containing C_D is of the form PΛ_D with P a height-one prime of 𝕀[[Γ^+_K]]; (ii) if M = M^+M^- with M^- squarefree with an odd number of prime factors, all inert in K, and ρ̄_𝐟 ramified at every ℓ | M^-, then no height-one prime of Λ_D contains both L^Σ_{𝐟,K,1} and C_D (SU Prop. 13.4.1).
hypotheses: The hypotheses of SU Prop. 12.2.5 on A; the auxiliary primes of Prop. 13.2.5 (a set of primes split in K not dividing the level) are part of the choice of Σ.
proofSteps: Express a Λ_D-combination of the c_D(β_i, x) as a product of Hecke L-values attached to auxiliary CM forms (SU §13.2–13.3, Props 13.2.5, 13.3.4).

Apply the mod-p nonvanishing results of Vatsal and Finis for anticyclotomic twists (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3h/finis-divisibility, mod-p-nonvanishing) to show that combination is not divisible by any height-one prime other than those pulled back from 𝕀[[Γ^+_K]].
Combine with L1/su-padic-l-function (iii), which excludes the pulled-back primes from L^Σ_{𝐟,K,1}, to get (ii).
acceptance: This is what makes ℰ_D nonzero modulo every height-one prime dividing L^Σ_{𝐟,K}, so that Thm 6.5.4 applies at those primes.

nodes.title: The four-dimensional pseudo-character of the ordinary GU(2,2) Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: For a neat K = K^0_pK^p ⊂ G(𝔸_f) and a finite set S of primes containing p and the primes where K_ℓ is not hyperspecial, there is a pseudo-representation T^S_{K^p}: G_K → h_{S,0}(K^p) of dimension four such that tr R_p(π) = λ^{ord}_π ∘ T^S_{K^p} for every p-ordinary cuspidal π of weight k with π_f^{K^p} ≠ 0 (SU Prop. 7.2.1), where R_p(π) is the four-dimensional Galois representation attached to π (imported from AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII: polarized, unramified outside S, crystalline at p when π_p is unramified, with the ordinary filtration at the primes above p). For a datum D, T_D is its composite with h_D, R_D the semisimple representation over the total fraction ring of h_D with trace T_D, and for each irreducible component J, R_J is either absolutely irreducible or, over a finite extension of Frac J, R_1 ⊕ R_2 with two-dimensional R_i satisfying R_i^c ≅ R_i^∨ ⊗ ε^{-3}ω^{1+c}_{K′} (SU Thm 7.3.1).
hypotheses: k regular for the attachment of R_p(π) (SU Thm 7.1.1, from Morel and Shin as explained in Skinner 2010); (irred)_𝐟 and (dist)_𝐟 for Thm 7.3.1.
The Galois representations of cuspidal representations of GU(2,2) and their local–global compatibility at p are imported (RT-AREA-iwasawa-1/6), not constructed here.
proofSteps: Define T(frob_v) := T_v (the Hecke operator giving −1 times the X^3-coefficient of the Hecke polynomial) for v ∉ S ∪ {p}, extend by continuity using Chebotarev density and compactness of h, and check independence of the approximating sequence on a Zariski-dense set of arithmetic points (proof of SU Prop. 7.2.1).
The pseudo-representation identities hold because they hold at each classical point and these are dense.

Thm 7.3.1: if R_J were a sum of two characters and an irreducible two-dimensional piece, specialize at a regular-weight point unramified at p to get a CAP representation, excluded by the residual shape tr ρ̄_D; otherwise R_J = R_1 ⊕ R_2 with the stated polarization.
acceptance: The residual pseudo-character of 𝕋_D is tr ρ̄_D: two characters and one irreducible two-dimensional constituent.

nodes.title: The Skinner–Urban Selmer lower bound from the Eisenstein ideal
nodes.statement: Assume (irred)_𝐟, (dist)_𝐟 and 𝕀 integrally closed. Let T = (T_𝐟 ⊗_𝕀 𝕀[[Γ_K]])(det ρ_𝐟^{-1}σ^{-c}_ξε^{-c}_K) with its ordinary summand T^+, and Ch^Σ_K(ρ_𝐟 ⊗ σ_ξε_K) ⊆ 𝕀[[Γ_K]] the characteristic ideal of X^Σ_K(T, T^+). For a height-one prime P_0 ⊂ 𝕀[[Γ_K]] with P = P_0Λ_D such that the four G_{K,p}-characters of SU (7.3.3.a) are residually distinct modulo P: (i) if ord_P(L^Σ_{χ̄_𝐟ξ̄′}) = 0 then ord_{P_0}(Ch^Σ_K(ρ_𝐟 ⊗ σ_ξε_K)) ≥ ord_P(𝔈_D) (SU Thm 7.3.3); (ii) if ℰ_D ≢ 0 modulo P and ord_P(L^Σ_{𝐟,K,ξ}) ≥ 1, then ord_P(Ch^Σ_K) ≥ 1, and if moreover ord_P(L^Σ_{χ̄_𝐟ξ̄′}) = 0 then ord_P(Ch^Σ_K) ≥ ord_P(L^Σ_{𝐟,K,ξ}) (SU Thm 7.3.5).
hypotheses: Residual disjointness (7.3.3.a) is verified in the proof of Thm 7.3.5: the four characters δ²_fσ^{-1}_{χ_f}ε_Wε, δ_fσ^{-1}_{χ_f}σ_ξε_W, δ_fσ^{-1}_{χ_f}σ^c_ξε_W, σ_{χ_f}ε^{-1}_Wσ^{-1}_{ξ′}ε are not ≡ 1 modulo P, by (dist)_𝐟 and a codimension count.
proofSteps: Set up the lattice datum of SU 7.3.2: A_0 = Λ_D, A = Λ̂_{D,P}, J_0 = 𝔈_D, R_0 = 𝕋_D, I_0 = I_D, V_0 = T_𝐟 ⊗ Λ_D, ρ_0 = ρ_𝐟 ⊗ σ_{χ̄_f,0}σ^{-c}_ξσ^c_ψε^{-2}, V^±_0 from T^+_𝐟, χ, χ′, ν, and σ from R_D.
Apply L0/lattice-construction (Prop. 4.5.6 and Cor. 4.5.7) and Shapiro (L0/sigma-primitive-selmer) to pass from ρ_0 ⊗ χ^{-1} over Λ_D to ρ_𝐟 ⊗ σ_ξε_K over 𝕀[[Γ_K]].
Thm 7.3.5 combines (i) with L1/padic-eisenstein-family (Thm 6.5.4) and checks (7.3.3.a).
acceptance: The bound is height-one-prime by height-one-prime and needs ℰ_D ≢ 0 mod P; L1/nonsingular-coefficient-coprimality supplies this at every P dividing L^Σ_{𝐟,K}.

nodes.title: Skinner–Urban's two-variable divisibility over K
nodes.statement: Let L ⊆ ℚ̄_p be a finite extension of ℚ_p containing ℚ[µ_{Np}, i, D_K^{1/2}], 𝕀 a normal domain finite over Λ_{W,O_L}, and 𝐟 an 𝕀-adic ordinary eigenform of tame level N with χ_𝐟 = 1. Suppose N = N^+N^- with N^+ divisible only by primes split in K and N^- only by primes inert in K, N^- squarefree with an odd number of prime factors, (irred)_𝐟 and (dist)_𝐟, and ρ̄_𝐟 ramified at every ℓ | N^-. For every finite Σ containing the primes dividing ND_K, Ch^Σ_{K_∞}(𝐟) ⊆ (L^Σ_{𝐟,K}) (SU Thm 3.6.1). For a classical p-ordinary eigenform f ∈ S_k(Np^r, χ; L), k ≥ 2, with χ = ω^{k−2}χ_1 (χ_1 of p-power order and conductor) and the same hypotheses, Ch^Σ_{K_∞,L}(f) ⊆ (L^Σ_{f,K}) (SU Cor. 3.6.2).
hypotheses: As stated; the hypotheses on N^- and ρ̄_𝐟|_{I_ℓ} enter through Vatsal's theorem (L1/su-padic-l-function (iii)); χ_𝐟 = 1 enters there and in the Galois argument; Σ ⊇ primes dividing ND_K avoids local–global compatibility away from p (SU remarks (i)–(v) after Thm 3.6.1).
proofSteps: For each height-one prime P_0 of 𝕀[[Γ_K]] dividing L^Σ_{𝐟,K}, choose the datum of L1/nonsingular-coefficient-coprimality so that ℰ_D ≢ 0 mod P = P_0Λ_D.

If ord_P L^Σ_{χ̄_𝐟ξ̄′} = 0 apply L1/su-selmer-lower-bound (ii); the Dirichlet factor is a unit at P because it lives in the cyclotomic variable only and P_0 is not pulled back (L1/su-padic-l-function (iii)).
Conclude ord_{P_0}(Ch^Σ) ≥ ord_{P_0}(L^Σ_{𝐟,K}) for every height-one P_0, hence the divisorial containment (end of SU §7, p. 108).
Cor. 3.6.2: specialize along 𝕀 → O_L using (3.3.12.b), L0/selmer-specialization-control (ii) and the comparison of L^Σ_{𝐟,K} with L^Σ_{f,K} (SU 3.4.6).
acceptance: Oriented: the characteristic ideal is contained in the ideal of the p-adic L-function (L divides the characteristic power series).
Integral, not after inverting p, under the stated hypotheses.

sources.locator: Thm 3.6.1 and remarks (i)–(v), pp. 41–42; Cor. 3.6.2 and proof, p. 42; end of §7, p. 108

nodes.title: Skinner–Urban's cyclotomic divisibility
nodes.statement: Let f ∈ S_k(Np^r, χ; L), k ≥ 2, be a p-ordinary cuspidal eigenform with (irred) and (dist) for ρ_f, χ = ω^{k−2}χ_1 with χ_1 of p-power order and conductor, and a prime q ≠ p with q ∥ N at which ρ̄_f is ramified; choose an imaginary quadratic K in which p splits, every prime dividing N/q splits and q is inert, so N^- = q. Then for every finite set of primes Σ, Ch^Σ_{ℚ_∞,L}(f)·Ch^Σ_{ℚ_∞,L}(f ⊗ χ_K) ⊆ (L^Σ_f·L^Σ_{f⊗χ_K}) (SU Cor. 3.6.3). This is the reverse divisibility exported to ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1/su-ordinary-theorem, in the normalization of the Σ-imprimitive ordinary Selmer dual and the canonical-period p-adic L-function; the equality (SU Thm 3.6.4, with Kato) is assembled there, not here.
hypotheses: As stated; the integral containment needs only these hypotheses. The integral equality additionally uses Kato's image condition (a basis with image containing SL₂(ℤ_p)), owned by the consumer.

The identification with ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0's ordinary Selmer dual and canonical-period p-adic L-function is made in that roadmap's range (trivial character, p ∤ N, the range of SU Thm 3.6.4); outside it the statement is about SU's own Σ-primitive Selmer group and L^Σ_f.
proofSteps: Reduce to Σ ∪ {p} containing all primes dividing ND_K (SU Lemma 3.2.17 and L0/primitive-imprimitive-comparison).

Apply L1/su-two-variable-theorem (Cor. 3.6.2), then descend from K_∞ to the cyclotomic line: L0/selmer-specialization-control (iii) (SU Prop. 3.2.11, Lemma 3.2.5, Cor. 3.2.9) gives Ch^Σ_{K^+_∞} = Ch^Σ_{ℚ_∞}(f)·Ch^Σ_{ℚ_∞}(f ⊗ χ_K) by Shapiro, and the restriction of L^Σ_{f,K} to Γ^+_K is L^Σ_f·L^Σ_{f⊗χ_K} up to unit (SU 3.4.6).
acceptance: Matches the request of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures for SU Thm 3.6.1 and Cor. 3.6.3 in its stated source range; the auxiliary field K is allowed to depend on f.

nodes.title: The semi-ordinary weight space and projector for GU(3,1)
nodes.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic with p = v_0v̄_0 split, and GU(3,1) the unitary similitude group of signature (3,1), so that GU(3,1)(ℚ_p) ≅ GL_4(ℚ_p) × ℚ_p^× and the diagonal torus of the p-adic group gives a four-coordinate p-adic weight space (after fixing the similitude character) of characters (a_1, a_2, a_3; b_1). The semi-ordinary torus T_so(ℤ_p) ⊂ T(ℤ_p) is the two-dimensional subtorus of weights (0, 0, t^+; t^-), with Iwasawa algebra Λ_so = ℤ_p[[T_so(1+pℤ_p)]]. On the p-adic forms V on the Igusa tower put U_p := U^+_{p,2}U^+_{p,3}U^-_{p,1}; for every f ∈ V the limit e_so f := lim_{r→∞} U_p^{r!} f exists and defines the semi-ordinary projector e_so. A classical form is semi-ordinary if it is fixed by e_so; this asks unit U_p-eigenvalues only in the two directions of T_so, so it allows forms whose GL_2 part at p is not ordinary (a_p = 0 is allowed). Keep the finite character of T_so(ℤ_p)/T_so(1+pℤ_p) when using the full group algebra; it is not another power-series variable.
hypotheses: p ≥ 3 split in K; the operators U^±_{p,i} are those of CLW (3.0.7)–(3.0.8) on p-integral forms.
The convergence of U_p^{r!} on every f uses the finiteness property (F) of CLW Thm 4.6.1, proved there; the generic profinite projector is imported.
proofSteps: Define U_p and verify property (F) for forms in V^♭ by CLW Prop. 3.0.2 and Prop. 4.5.2, and for all of V by Prop. 4.5.3.
Apply the profinite ordinary projector of PadicFamilies:L0a to the locally finite endomorphism U_p to obtain e_so.
acceptance: Semi-ordinary is weaker than ordinary: an ordinary form is semi-ordinary, while a form whose GL_2 constituent at p has a_p = 0 can be semi-ordinary and is killed by the ordinary projector.

nodes.title: Semi-ordinary Hida theory and the fundamental exact sequence
nodes.statement: With e_so as in L2s/semi-ordinary-weight-space: (1) the duals V^{0,*}_so = Hom(e_so V^0, ℚ_p/ℤ_p) and V^*_so = Hom(e_so V, ℚ_p/ℤ_p) are free of finite rank over Λ_so (vertical control, CLW Thm 3.0.7 for cusp forms, Thm 4.6.1 for all forms); (2) the spaces of Λ_so-families of tame level K^p_f, M^0_so = Hom_{Λ_so}(V^{0,*}_so, Λ_so) and M_so = Hom_{Λ_so}(V^*_so, Λ_so), specialize isomorphically at every weight (τ^+, τ^-) with 0 ≥ t^+ ≥ −t^- + 4 onto the limits of e_so-parts of mod p^m forms of that weight, and classical semi-ordinary forms embed into the specialization after inverting p (CLW (2.9.1)); (3) Thm 2.9.1(4) gives the exact sequence 0→M_so^0→M_so→⊕_g M_(0,0)(K′_{f,g};Z_p)⊗_Zp Z_p[[T_so(Z_p)]]→0. Thus the boundary uses the full torus group algebra, with its finite-character action. Only after the specified ξ/Γ_K base change does one obtain the boundary form used in Thm 8.1.1. Thm 2.9.1(3) gives surjectivity onto classical cuspidal forms for t^-≥A(t^+); this extra condition is not automatic from the cone in (2).
hypotheses: The weights in (2) satisfy 0 ≥ t^+ ≥ −t^- + 4; for the Klingen family, 0 ≫ t^+ ≫ −t^-.
The Shimura variety of GU(3,1), its toroidal and minimal compactifications, the Igusa tower and the boundary strata are imported from AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L4 and AutomorphicBundles.
Retain the finite torus character when passing from Λ_so to the full boundary group algebra. Classical cusp-surjectivity additionally requires t^-≥A(t^+).
proofSteps: Base change and q-expansion: CLW Props 3.0.1–3.0.6; vertical control for cusp forms (Thm 3.0.7).

The boundary: restriction to the strata Z_{g,n} gives the exact sequences (4.4.2)–(4.4.3) with the Siegel operators Φ_g (Prop. 4.4.1), whose global sections are forms on the zero-dimensional Shimura variety of GU(2).
Finiteness (F) and the vertical control for all forms (Props 4.5.1–4.5.3, Thm 4.6.1); combine into Thm 2.9.1.
acceptance: The exactness on the right is what allows a Λ_so-adic lift of the boundary values of the Klingen family, hence a cuspidal family congruent to it.

nodes.title: The semi-ordinary Klingen Eisenstein family on GU(3,1)
nodes.statement: Let π and ξ satisfy CLW §5.2: π is weight two, each π_v is unramified, Steinberg or its unramified quadratic twist, π_p is unramified, some nonsplit q has π_q ramified, π is ramified at 2 if 2 is nonsplit, ρ̄_π|G_K is irreducible, and ξ has infinity type (0,k_0) with k_0 even. CLW addendum Thm 4.0.1 constructs two families E^{Kling}_i (i=1,2) in the specified space of ♮ semi-ordinary measures tensored with Q. They use different auxiliary data, have the same unramified/U_p eigensystem, and specialize to the semi-ordinary holomorphic Klingen series at ξτ of type (0,k), k≥6 even. Every constant term of either family is divisible by L^{Σ∪{ℓ,ℓ′}}_{ξ,Q}L^{Σ∪{ℓ,ℓ′}}_{π,K,ξ} in R[1/p], R=O_L^{ur}[[Γ_K]]. No integral unscaled measure or single-family unit coefficient is asserted.
hypotheses: Use the two auxiliary data sets of CLW addendum §3, not the original simultaneous-unit choice. The weakened ℓ-tower nonvanishing and the additional finite-set avoidance there are required.

The Siegel Eisenstein measures on unitary groups, the pullback formula and the local doubling integrals are imported from AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L4 and L4e (Eischen–Wan's ordinary U(3,1) family is their r = 2 case); CLW's semi-ordinary sections at p, which replace Eischen–Wan's ordinary ones, and the Klingen choices are owned here.
proofSteps: Choose the quaternion transfer and two local auxiliary data sets as in the addendum §§2–3. Its weakened nonvanishing suffices to make two selected factors units for each set, rather than all three for one set.
Interpolate the Siegel Eisenstein series on GU(3,3) into a measure (Thm 5.9.1) and pull back along GU(3,1) × GU(0,2) ↪ GU(3,3) against π_D (Thm 5.5.1, doubling formula), applying e_so (Prop. 5.10.1).

Use the local calculations of CLW §§5–7 and addendum Thm 4.0.1: both ♮ measure families have the same eigensystem and the specified constant-term divisibility in R[1/p]. CLW’s nonordinary p-sections are owned here; the ordinary local-zeta-at-p supplier does not supply them.
acceptance: Shared local test data: the sections at p and the auxiliary characters are fixed before any arithmetic conclusion, and FW's general-weight family (L2/vector-valued-klingen-family) reuses them.

Then J is contained in no height-one prime of R[1/p]. This does not assert that either single family has a unit coefficient or that J is the unit ideal. The local expansions, triple-product identities and Rallis pairings are those of CLW §7; the addendum replaces the original auxiliary-unit choice.

Restrict to (N·U(2)) × U(2), pair with θ⋆ and then with h via the doubling formula; the result is a triple product integral ∫ h θ f (Props 7.6.1, 7.7.1).

Apply addendum Thm 4.0.1: after its finite integral coefficient extension and power map, J contains, up to units, the nonzero factors L_{1,1} and L_{6,2} in independent rank-one directions. They have no common height-one prime. Descend this assertion along the finite integral extension; it gives height-one avoidance for J in R[1/p].

nodes.title: The CLW Eisenstein ideal is bounded by the p-adic L-functions
nodes.statement: Let ϕ be as in CLW Prop. 7.11.2 and E_{π,ξ} ⊆ Ô^{ur}_L[[Γ_K]] the Eisenstein ideal (L0/eisenstein-ideal) of the semi-ordinary cuspidal Hecke algebra 𝕋^0_{so,ξ,Γ_K} for the eigensystem of E^{Kling}_ϕ. For every height-one prime P of Ô^{ur}_L[[Γ_K]] with P ∩ Ô^{ur}_L = 0, ord_P(L^{Σ∪{ℓ,ℓ′}}_{π,K,ξ}·L^{Σ∪{ℓ,ℓ′}}_{ξ,ℚ}) ≤ ord_P(E_{π,ξ}) (CLW Thm 8.1.1).

proofSteps: Fix P∤p and choose one of the two families with a Fourier–Jacobi functional value outside P (addendum Thm 5.0.1). Use the fundamental exact sequence to lift its boundary values divided by L_{π,K,ξ}L_{ξ,Q} modulo P^r.
Subtract to obtain a cuspidal family modulo P^r; its chosen functional value is a P-unit, so the congruence class is nonzero.
The eigensystem therefore yields E_{π,ξ}⊂P^r locally for r=ord_P(L·L); hence ord_P(E_{π,ξ})≥r. The original proof’s final ≤ sign on PDF p. 78 is reversed, while its theorem statement is correct.
acceptance: The bound is height-one prime by height-one prime and excludes P ∋ p; it is one-sided.

nodes.title: Irreducibility of the GU(3,1) pseudo-character: excluding CAP components
nodes.statement: Let 𝕋 be the semi-ordinary (or ordinary) cuspidal Hecke algebra of GU(3,1) localized at the Eisenstein maximal ideal, T: G_K → 𝕋 its four-dimensional pseudo-character (built as in L1/gu22-galois-pseudocharacter from the Galois representations of cuspidal representations of U(3,1)), and suppose ρ̄_π|_{G_K} is irreducible. Then for every Frac(A)-algebra map λ: 𝕋 ⊗ Frac(A) → K′, the representation σ_λ is absolutely irreducible or contains an absolutely irreducible two-dimensional subrepresentation whose trace is ≡ χ + χ′ (with χ′=χ^{-c} here because ν=1) modulo I — Wan20's property (9) (CLW proof of Thm 8.2.1). If instead T = δ_1 + δ_2 + δ_3 with δ_3 two-dimensional and residually tr ρ̄_π, then at an arithmetic point x of weight (0,0,t^+;t^-) with 0 ≫ t^+ ≫ −t^-, a twist of the specialization of δ_3 descends to a G_ℚ-representation ρ′_{3,x} which is modular (ordinary case: as in SU Thm 7.3.1; non-ordinary case: ρ_Π|_{G_{K,p}} is crystalline by a Jacquet-module argument and the semi-ordinary slopes, and Kisin's theorem applies; in general weight FW uses Pan's theorem), so Π is CAP, which Harris's Thm 2.5.6 excludes in these weights.
hypotheses: ρ̄_π|_{G_K} irreducible; arithmetic points in the absolutely convergent range of sufficiently regular weight.
The unitary forms and Hecke operators are the AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L4 carriers; the semi-ordinary projector is L2s's own, since L4 plans only the ordinary one.
Harris (1984) Thm 2.5.6 (no holomorphic CAP forms of these weights on U(3,1)) is an input not planned in the atlas (gap 'harris-cap').
proofSteps: Suppose the pseudo-character is a sum δ_1 + δ_2 + δ_3; residual irreducibility of ρ̄_π gives a two-dimensional 𝕋-valued representation for δ_3.
Ordinary π: the specialization of δ_3 at x is ordinary and modular by the SU argument.

Non-ordinary π: Edixhoven makes ρ̄_π|_{G_{ℚ_p}} irreducible; Jacquet modules show Π_p is an unramified principal series (the semi-ordinary valuations (8.2.4)–(8.2.5) force distinct ratios ≠ p^{±1}), so ρ_Π|_{G_{K,p}} and ρ′_{3,x} are crystalline; ρ̄′_{3,x} is not induced from ℚ(√p*), so Kisin's modularity lifting applies (FW: Pan's Fontaine–Mazur theorem for de Rham ρ with ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}} absolutely irreducible).
Modularity of ρ′_{3,x} makes Π CAP (Klingen type), contradicting Harris Thm 2.5.6 for the chosen weights.
acceptance: Shared by L2s/clw-main-divisibility and L2/fw-greenberg-divisibility; the RT-AREA-iwasawa-1/6 addendum asks exactly for these GL₂ modularity and Harris inputs.

nodes.title: The Castella–Liu–Wan divisibility over the cyclotomic-localized ring
nodes.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic, p ≥ 3 split in K, and π, ξ as in CLW §5.2. Let Γ^+_K ⊂ Γ_K be the rank-one ℤ_p-submodule on which complex conjugation acts by +1 and R := O^{ur}_L[[Γ_K]] ⊗_{O_L[[Γ^+_K]]} Frac(O_L[[Γ^+_K]]), the localization inverting every nonzero element of the cyclotomic coefficient subring O_L[[Γ^+_K]]. Then, as fractional ideals of R, (L_{π,K,ξ}) ⊇ char_R(X^{ur}_{π,K,ξ} ⊗_{A} R), where X_{π,K,ξ} is the dual of the Selmer group of T_{π,K,ξ} = T_π(ε^2_{cyc})|_{G_K}(ξ^{-1}) ⊗ ℤ_p[[Γ_K]](Ψ^{-1}_K) with relaxed condition at p, unramified condition at p̄, and unramified conditions at every place away from p (CLW Thm 8.2.1(1)). The localization is in the cyclotomic subring; it is not the inversion of p. Here A=O_L^{ur}[[Γ_K]] and X^{ur} denotes extension to A first. The final tensor is over A; tensoring the A-module X again over the smaller cyclotomic subring would duplicate variables. This localization also inverts p, but inverts many additional elements.
hypotheses: CLW §5.2; the excluded height-one primes are exactly those with P ∩ O_L[[Γ^+_K]] ≠ 0 (pulled back from the cyclotomic line) — in particular primes where (X_{ξ∘Nm} ⊗ ℚ)_P ≠ 0 may be among them.
If X_{π,K,ξ} is not torsion its characteristic ideal is 0 and the statement is empty.
proofSteps: Reduce to the Σ ∪ {ℓ,ℓ′}-primitive inclusion (L0/primitive-imprimitive-comparison; JSW Thm 6.1.6 and Greenberg–Vatsal Prop. 2.4).

For P with P ∩ O_L[[Γ^+_K]] = 0, the inequality ord_P(L) ≤ length(X_P) follows from ord_P(E_{π,ξ}) ≤ length(X_P) by L2s/clw-eisenstein-congruence (L_{ξ,ℚ} lives in the cyclotomic variable, hence is a unit at P).

Set up the lattice datum (1)–(5) with ν trivial, χ = ξΨ_K, ρ from ρ_π, σ the pseudo-representation of the semi-ordinary Hecke algebra, I = E_{π,ξ}A_P; check (6)–(8) as in Wan20 and (9) by L2s/cap-exclusion; apply L0/lattice-construction (Wan20 Prop. 9.2) where ord_P(E_{π,ξ}) > 0 and (X_{ξ∘Nm} ⊗ ℚ)_P = 0.
acceptance: The statement is one-sided and localized; neither torsion of X nor equality is proved here.
Height-one primes pulled back from O_L[[Γ^+_K]] are not controlled: CLW cannot prove the analogue of Wan20 Lemma 9.3 with π fixed.

nodes.title: Integrality of the CLW p-adic L-function and the p-inverted divisibility
nodes.statement: In the setting of L2s/clw-main-divisibility: (a) if ξ_p ≢ ξ_p̄ modulo the maximal ideal of O_L, then L_{π,K,ξ} ∈ O^{ur}_L[[Γ_K]]; (b) if moreover ξ|_{𝔸_ℚ^×} = ω² (ω the Teichmüller character) with k_0 ≡ 0 mod 2(p − 1), the local base-change root number ε_v(1/2, BC(π) × ξ_0) equals 1 at every finite place v nonsplit in K, and the conductor of ξ is divisible only by primes split in K, then (L_{π,K,ξ}) ⊇ char_{O^{ur}_L[[Γ_K]] ⊗ ℚ}(X_{π,K,ξ} ⊗ ℚ) (CLW Thm 8.2.1(2)): the containment holds after inverting p, without the cyclotomic localization. This is the source-qualified input that RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.6a imports for its supersingular branch; it is not a nonordinary equality.

(b) adds the four listed conditions; the containment is only after ⊗ ℚ.

Use the CM-theta comparison contract of L0/hida-tilouine-anticyclotomic: CLW p. 81 invokes HT93 Thm 7.1 and (8.8b), Hid91 Lemma 5.3(vi), and HT93/HT94/Hid06. Their exact integral congruence-ideal/Katz dictionary remains hida-tilouine-not-read; no general CM-field theorem is asserted here.

(b): Hsieh's vanishing of the anticyclotomic µ-invariant shows L_{π,K,ξ} lies in no height-one prime pulled back from O_L[[Γ^+_K]] other than possibly (p), so combining with L2s/clw-main-divisibility the excluded primes contribute nothing after inverting p.

nodes.title: Semi-ordinary Hida theory on GU(3,1) in general weight
nodes.statement: For f a normalized cuspidal eigenform of even weight k ≥ 2 and the vector-valued semi-ordinary forms on GU(3,1) of weight k = (a_1, a_2, a_3; b_1) in the family set X_ρ of Fouquet–Wan: the semi-ordinary parts e_α·V_k(K_0(p,p^n)) are p-divisible with uniformly bounded classical dimensions (Props 7.9–7.10); for each weight k = (a_1, a_2, a_3; b_1) ∈ X_ρ there is A(a) such that, for b_1 large compared with A(a), the restriction e_α M_k(K_0(p), O) ⊗ ℚ_p/ℤ_p → e_α·V_k(K_0(p)) is an isomorphism (FW Thm 7.11); for q = 0 or ∅ the Λ̃-adic families V^q_so are free of finite rank and M^q_so(K, Λ̃) ⊗ Λ̃/P_k ≅ e_α M^q_k(K, O) at such weights (Thm 7.12), with Thm 7.15 and the weight-k boundary sequence of Thm 7.17; and the short sequence of cusp forms, forms and boundary forms is exact (Thm 7.18). These extend L2s/semi-ordinary-hida-theory (CLW, weight two) to general weight and are the only new Hida-theoretic input L2 owns.

Fix ρ=(a_1,a_2). The full torus algebra has four variables; the fixed-ρ family varies (a_3,b_1). Thm 7.11 requires b_1>A(a,n); Thm 7.12 identifies classical specializations only in its sufficiently regular range.
Prop. 7.13 additionally assumes ρ̄_f|G_Qp irreducible, a_1=a_2=0, a_3≡b_1≡0 mod p−1, and a_2−a_3 and a_3+b_1 sufficiently large; its conclusion gives the required unramified principal-series points.
proofSteps: Vertical control for the vector-valued sheaves (FW Props 7.5, 7.7–7.10) following CLW §§3–4.
Uniform boundedness of dimensions and classicality (Thm 7.11, Prop. 7.13).
Freeness and the boundary exact sequence (Thms 7.12, 7.15, 7.17, 7.18), with the Siegel operators of L2s.

nodes.title: The vector-valued Klingen Eisenstein family and the Greenberg p-adic L-function
nodes.statement: Let π = π_f be the unitary automorphic representation of a weight-k form f and Σ a finite set containing the bad primes. (i) There is L^Σ_{f,K,ξ_0} ∈ Λ_{K,O^{ur}} ⊗ ℚ_p interpolating, at characters ξ_φ of Γ_K that are avatars of Hecke characters of conductor p and infinity type (κ_φ/2 + m_φ, −κ_φ/2 − m_φ) with κ_φ ≥ 6 even and m_φ ≥ (k−2)/2, the values L^Σ(π̃, ξ_φ, (κ_φ − 1)/2) times the stated periods and local factors (FW Prop. 7.19(i), from Eischen–Wan Thm 1.2); (ii) there is a family of formal q-expansions E_{f,ξ_0} whose specializations at a Zariski-dense set of arithmetic points are the Fourier–Jacobi expansions of the highest weight vectors of the holomorphic vector-valued Klingen Eisenstein series on GU(3,1) built by the pullback formula, eigen for U_{t+} with nonzero eigenvalue (Prop. 7.19(ii)); (iii) the constant terms a_{t,[g]}(0) are divisible by L^Σ_{f,K,ξ_0}·L^Σ_{τ̄′} (Prop. 7.19(iii)). After the reparametrization t^{-c}_{ξ′_0}, L^{Gr,Σ}_{f,K} := t^{-c}_{ξ′_0}(L_{f,K,ξ_0}) is the Greenberg Rankin–Selberg p-adic L-function, it equals L^{Hida}_{f⊗g}·L^{Katz}_K·h_K (FW Cor. 7.21, L2/greenberg-function-factorization) and lies in O^{ur}[[Γ_K]] (FW Lemma 7.22). The multiplier in Prop. 7.19(i) is Ω_p^{4m+2κ}/Ω_∞^{4m+2κ} · c′_φ · p^{κ−3} · g(ξ_{φ,2})² · ∏_{i=1}²(χ_i^{-1}ξ_{φ,2}^{-1})(p), where Lemma 7.20 gives c′_φ=Γ(κ+m−k/2)Γ(κ+m+k/2−1)2^{−3κ−4m+1}π^{1−2κ−2m}i^{k−κ−2m−1}. The highest weight is (m+(k−2)/2,m−(k−2)/2,0;κ); after reparametrization it is ((k−2)/2,−(k−2)/2,−m;κ+m).
hypotheses: Eischen–Wan's distinct-Satake-parameter assumption is unnecessary in the U(2) case (FW remark after Prop. 7.19).
The Klingen family of Eischen–Wan (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L4e) is the analytic carrier; FW's reparametrization, the Ikeda-type archimedean factorization and the integrality are owned here.
proofSteps: Translate Eischen–Wan Thm 1.2 to the semi-ordinary GU(3,1) setting with the shared local data of L2s/semi-ordinary-klingen-family (FW Prop. 7.19).
Reparametrize by t^{-c}_{ξ′_0} (γ′ ↦ γ′ξ′_0(γ′)^{-1}, then γ′ ↦ γ′^{-c}).

Apply FW Lemma 7.22 with its two independent denominator bounds: one supported at p and the explicit Euler factors and one in the CM-family variable. Prove that these supports are disjoint using that lemma; a nonzero rational scalar alone does not prove integrality.
acceptance: Only the vector-valued, general-weight construction is new here; the weight-two scalar family is L2s's.

nodes.title: Factorization of the Greenberg function into Hida and Katz factors
nodes.statement: With the normalizations of FW §4.5.2 and Appendix B, the Greenberg Rankin–Selberg p-adic L-function of f over K factors as L^{Gr}_K(f) = L^{Hida}_{f⊗g}·L^{Katz}_K·h_K, where L^{Hida}_{f⊗g} is Hida's Rankin–Selberg p-adic L-function of f against the canonical CM Hida family g, L^{Katz}_K is Katz's p-adic L-function of K restricted to the relevant line and h_K the class number factor (FW Cor. 7.21, with Prop. 4.35 for the Katz normalization). The factorization is an identity in Frac(O^{ur}[[Γ_K]]) obtained by comparing interpolation formulas on a Zariski-dense set; it carries the class-number, period and local factors explicitly and is not routed to L5a.

proofSteps: Compare interpolation formulas at the arithmetic points of Prop. 7.19 using the doubling interpolation on one side and Hida's Rankin–Selberg plus Katz's interpolation on the other (FW Lemma before Cor. 7.21).
Density of the comparison points and the Weierstrass preparation in O^{ur}[[Γ_K]] give the identity.

nodes.title: General-weight Fourier–Jacobi comparison and its auxiliary repair contract
nodes.statement: Conditional original formula: with the auxiliary data of FW Prop. 7.29, if L_1,L_5,L_6 are simultaneously units and L_2 is a fixed nonzero scalar, FJ_{h,β,θ⋆}(E^{Kling}) is a unit times an element of Q̄_p^×. This only excludes height-one primes away from p. Together with Thm 7.18, the original argument yields ord_P(L^{Gr,Σ}_{f,K})≤ord_P(𝔈_D) for the admissible P≠(p) of Lemma 7.31. The cited auxiliary nonvanishing no longer proves the simultaneous-unit hypothesis: the CLW addendum replaces it in weight two by two families whose functional values jointly avoid every height-one prime of R[1/p]. A vector-valued, general-weight version of that repair is required here; it is an explicit gap, not a consequence of the scalar weight-two theorem.

The weakened auxiliary ℓ-tower nonvanishing must instead be used in a general-weight version of the CLW two-family argument.

Ichino's formula evaluates the resulting triple product as L_3L_4 times Rallis inner products (interpolated by L_3, L_4) and local integrals; the ratio to L_1L_2L_5L_6 is a fixed nonzero constant (FW Prop. 7.29). This evaluation does not by itself establish the simultaneous-unit choice.

Adapt CLW addendum Thms 4.0.1 and 5.0.1 to the vector-valued family and its archimedean functional. Prove that the two auxiliary values have independent variable supports and their joint ideal avoids height-one primes after inverting p. Only after that missing step may the congruence argument establish Lemma 7.31 unconditionally in this plan.

nodes.title: Fouquet–Wan's GU(3,1) divisibility for the Greenberg main conjecture
nodes.statement: Let f be a normalized cuspidal eigenform of even weight k, trivial character and conductor N prime to p, such that either ρ̄_f|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is absolutely irreducible or f is ordinary at p; suppose every prime q | N nonsplit in K satisfies q ∥ N and there is at least one such q, that 2 ∥ N if 2 is nonsplit in K, and that ρ̄_f is absolutely irreducible over G_K. Then char_{O^{ur}[[Γ_K]]}(X^{Gr}_K(f) ⊗_O O^{ur}) ⊆ (L^{Gr}_K(f)) up to height-one primes pulled back from O[[Γ^+]]; if moreover every ℓ | N nonsplit in K is ramified in K with π_ℓ the Steinberg representation twisted by the unramified character sending ℓ to −ℓ^{k/2−1}, the whole containment holds (FW Thm 7.32 = Thm 4.41 = Thm 1.12). Here X^{Gr}_K(f) is the dual of the Greenberg Rankin–Selberg Selmer group (FW Def. 4.39: Greenberg condition at v_0, strict at v̄_0, unramified-quotient conditions away from p).

The first containment excludes height-one primes pulled back from O[[Γ^+]]; the second needs the Steinberg-twist hypothesis to invoke the anticyclotomic µ = 0 theorem.
This is the source theorem target. The roadmap proof remains partial pending general-weight-nonvanishing-repair; the later scalar CLW repair alone does not discharge it.

Lemma 7.31 (L2/fw-fourier-jacobi-unit) bounds ord_P(L^{Gr,Σ}) ≤ ord_P(𝔈_D) for P ≠ (p).
Put back the Euler factors at Σ (Greenberg–Vatsal Prop. 2.4; K_∞ contains the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension; L0/primitive-imprimitive-comparison).

Under the Steinberg hypothesis apply Hsieh's anticyclotomic µ = 0 to see that L^{Gr}_K(f) lies in no height-one prime of O[[Γ^+]], hence is prime to the Dirichlet factor in the constant terms (L2/exceptional-height-one-primes).

nodes.title: Removing the excluded height-one primes
nodes.statement: Let L ∈ O^{ur}[[Γ_K]] be L^{Gr}_K(f) (or Wan's L_{f,K,ξ}). If the anticyclotomic restriction of L has vanishing µ-invariant — which holds when every prime ℓ | N nonsplit in K is ramified in K with π_ℓ the appropriately twisted Steinberg representation and the residual and conductor hypotheses of Hsieh's Theorem B are met — then L lies in no height-one prime of O^{ur}[[Γ_K]] of the form Q·O^{ur}[[Γ_K]] with Q a height-one prime of O[[Γ^+]]; hence it is prime to the cyclotomic Dirichlet factor L^Σ_{τ̄′} of the constant terms, and a divisibility proved up to those pulled-back primes extends over them (any independent p-power ambiguity must also be removed). For a Hida family, Wan20 Lemma 9.3 gives the same conclusion; for a single form outside the µ = 0 range the exceptional primes remain excluded.
hypotheses: Hypotheses of AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3h/theorem-b (Hsieh's µ = 0) for the anticyclotomic specialization; the auxiliary-field choice of L2/auxiliary-field-selection must preserve them (no nonsplit-prime or minimality condition dropped).

nodes.title: The universal deformation ring is a reduced complete intersection, finite free over Λ, and equal to the Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: Under FW Assumption 2.1 (L3/fw-residual-hypotheses), the universal deformation ring R_Σ(ρ̄) of ρ̄ unramified outside Σ is a flat O-algebra which is a complete intersection of Krull dimension 4 (FW Prop. 2.4); there is a Zariski-dense open X^sm ⊂ Spec R_Σ(ρ̄) containing every point that is ordinary up to twist (if ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is reducible) or crystalline and short up to twist (if irreducible), at which Spec R^χ_Σ(ρ̄) → Spec O is formally smooth, and R_Σ(ρ̄) is reduced (Cor. 2.5); the classical points (up to twist) are Zariski dense, so the surjection R_Σ(ρ̄) → 𝕋^Σ_{m_ρ̄} is an isomorphism (Prop. 2.6); and there is a regular sequence (x_1, x_2, x_3) in 𝕋^Σ_{m_ρ̄} making it a finite free module over Λ = O[[X_1, X_2, X_3]], such that classical points with the same image in Spec Λ are all crystalline-short (resp. ordinary) up to twist or none are (Cor. 2.7). Finite flatness over the regular ring Λ does not make R_Σ(ρ̄) regular; the main conjecture over R_Σ(ρ̄) is formulated through perfect complexes and the regular subring Λ.
hypotheses: FW Assumption 2.1; p odd; Σ finite containing p and the ramification of ρ̄.
The existence of a classical point of the Serre weight (FW cites Edixhoven/Gross–Coleman–Voloch-type results [31]) and the local deformation rings at p (ordinary or crystalline-short) are inputs.
The complete-intersection and density proof here is FW Prop. 2.4–2.6 with its local hypotheses. Do not replace it by the supplier’s unobstructed-ring hypothesis or assume all such rings regular.
proofSteps: Twisting by canonical square roots of characters in 1 + ϖO identifies R_Σ(ρ̄) ≅ R^χ_Σ(ρ̄) ⊗̂ R_Σ(𝟙), reducing to fixed determinant (proof of FW Prop. 2.4).

Fixed determinant: the ordinary (resp. crystalline-short) quotient is cut out by a regular sequence (x_2, x_3) and is a finite Hecke algebra at a classical point; a presentation over the local rings gives the complete-intersection property (GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.3/local-to-global-presentation, global-dimension-lower-bound).

Use FW Cor. 2.5 and Prop. 2.6: establish reducedness and density with the specified ordinary/crystalline local quotients, then identify R with T. R31.6/boeckle-r-equals-t supplies a related unobstructed statement; it does not prove this obstructed complete-intersection theorem on its own.
Choose x_1 from R_Σ(𝟙) to get the Λ-structure of Cor. 2.7.
acceptance: The Λ-structure depends on the initial classical point; the map Spec 𝕋 → Spec Λ may be ramified, even at classical points, but not at points of X^sm.
No axiom 'R = T' is imported: the isomorphism is proved from density of classical points and reducedness.

sources.locator: Prop. 2.4 and proof, p. 18; Cor. 2.5, p. 19; Prop. 2.6 and Cor. 2.7 with proofs, p. 20
sources.match: Flatness and the complete-intersection property, the smooth locus X^sm, R = 𝕋 and the finite free Λ-structure.
R_Σ(ρ̄) ≅ 𝕋 is a reduced complete intersection of relative dimension 3, not known to be factorial; the descent is carried out over the regular ring Λ.

nodes.title: Classical points of good reduction type exist and are dense
nodes.statement: Under FW Assumption 2.1: (i) if ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is irreducible there is a crystalline and short classical point λ_f with R_Σ(ρ̄) ≅ R_Σ(ρ̄_f) (FW Lemma 2.2), and in general a point of Spec 𝕋^Σ_{m_ρ̄} that is crystalline-short, crystalline-short up to the quadratic twist ω^{(p−1)/2}, good ordinary, or good ordinary up to a quadratic twist (FW Lemma 2.8, used in the proof of Thm 5.1); (ii) X^sm is Zariski dense and the set of specializations that are not Iwasawa-suitable, or at which Spec 𝕋 is not étale over Spec Λ, is contained in a locus of codimension at least one (FW Props 2.6, 3.16).
hypotheses: As stated; Iwasawa-suitable in the sense of FW Def. 3.19.
proofSteps: Lemma 2.2: twist so that the inertial weights are fundamental characters of level 2 and use the Serre weight conjecture (now a theorem) to produce a crystalline short form.
Lemma 2.8: the analogous statement covering the reducible-at-p case with ordinary points.
Density and codimension from Cor. 2.5 and Prop. 3.16.
acceptance: These are the seed points at which L4/etale-point-descent applies L2's crystalline theorem or the ordinary theorem.

nodes.title: Fundamental lines over the deformation ring and its quotients
nodes.statement: Let A be a quotient of 𝕋^Σ_{m_ρ̄} or of Λ (for example 𝕋, R(𝔞) = 𝕋/𝔞 for a minimal prime 𝔞, Λ, O_Iw or O) and T := T_Σ ⊗ A. The complexes RΓ_et(ℤ[1/Σ], T) and RΓ(G_{ℚ_ℓ}, T) are perfect and commute with derived base change (FW Lemma 3.17). The Σ-partial fundamental line is the graded invertible A-module Δ_Σ(T) := Det^{-1}_A RΓ_et(ℤ[1/Σ], T) ⊗_A Det^{-1}_A T(−1)^+ (FW Def. 3.18); for A a domain and ℓ ∈ Σ prime to p put X_ℓ(T) := Det_A RΓ(G_{ℚ_ℓ}/I_ℓ, T^{I_ℓ}) if rank T^{I_ℓ} ≠ 1 and Det_A[A —(1−α_ℓ)→ A] if rank T^{I_ℓ} = 1, and the fundamental line Δ(T) := Δ_Σ(T) ⊗ ⊗_{ℓ∈Σ∖{p}}(X_ℓ(T) ⊗ Det^{-1}_A RΓ(G_{ℚ_ℓ}, T)). Any ψ: A → A′ induces Δ_A(T) ⊗_A A′ ≅ Δ_{A′}(T′) for the Σ-partial line, and for the full line when ψ is Iwasawa-suitable; when both are defined, Δ_A(T) ≅ Det^{-1}RΓ_et(ℤ[1/p], T) ⊗ Det^{-1}T(−1)^+ (FW Prop. 3.20). In the rank-one correction [A→(1−α_ℓ)A], the two terms are in degrees 0 and 1. Under the acyclic trivialization its determinant basis maps to 1−α_ℓ; the inverse determinant gives (1−α_ℓ)^{-1}. No local X_p is used.
hypotheses: Use the requested Knudsen–Mumford graded determinant functor on perfect complexes, owned by PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L5 but not present in the current upstream checkout; T(−1)^+ is the complex-conjugation + part.
proofSteps: Perfectness and base change of étale cohomology complexes (Nekovář's Selmer complexes, FW Lemma 3.17).
Define Δ_Σ and Δ by the determinant functor; the local factors X_ℓ use the explicit two-term complex when the inertia invariants have rank one.

Prop. 3.20: identify Δ with the {p}-partial line through the cone of RΓ(ℤ[1/Σ]) ⊕ ⊕RΓ(G_{ℚ_ℓ}) → ⊕RΓ(G_{ℚ_ℓ}/I_ℓ, T^{I_ℓ}), and check base change of X_ℓ when ranks of inertia invariants agree and ψ(α_ℓ) = α′_ℓ.
acceptance: Fitting ideals commute with ordinary module base change but need not be invertible and do not encode the alternating determinant of all cohomology. Characteristic divisors require the appropriate normal-ring hypotheses and are principal only in a UFD. Perfect-complex determinant lines commute with derived base change; the full local correction also requires Iwasawa-suitability.

nodes.title: Completed (co)homology localized at ρ̄ and its local–global factorization
nodes.statement: Under Nakamura (N1),(N3),(N4), use the intrinsic BM co-Whittaker factor B_{Σ_0} and its smooth dual B^∨_{Σ_0}. In NAK-v2 Cor. 2.5 (p. 25), completed Borel–Moore homology factors as (π_p^m)^*⊗(ρ^m)^*⊗B_{Σ_0}; the factor is the untilde π of that version. NAK-v2 Thm 2.2 (p. 20) describes completed cohomology using the smooth-dual factor, denoted tilde π there. The published version reverses these notational roles. The zeta construction uses the BM factor as in NAK-v2 (47), p. 63; do not identify B with B^∨. In the GL₂ families used by FW Props 6.7–6.9, the specified essential-vector level has free rank-one invariants with the stated classical base change. This last property uses the explicit GL₂ classification, not merely the rank-one top derivative in the definition of co-Whittaker.
hypotheses: (N1), (N3), (N4); in particular p ≥ 5, which is the range of PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp:R30.5's nodes. FW's extension to p = 3 rests on Paškūnas–Tung's generalization (FW remark after Thm 3.6), which the imported nodes do not cover; the request to R30.5 asks for it. The co-Whittaker families exist (Helm's local Langlands in families, conditional in general in SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.5, proved in the GL_2 cases needed by FW Prop. 6.8).
proofSteps: Import Emerton's local–global compatibility (CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility:R31.4) and the Paškūnas description of the Montréal functor (PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp:R30.5).

Use NAK-v2 Cor. 2.5 for BM homology and its untilde co-Whittaker factor; use Thm 2.2 for cohomology and the smooth-dual factor. Track the factors by their intrinsic property before importing notation from the published version.
Essential vectors in families: co-Whittaker modules are unique (FW Prop. 6.7), have the explicit shapes of Prop. 6.8, and their K_1(ϖ^m)-invariants are free of rank one with base change (Prop. 6.9).
acceptance: R31.4 and R30.5/R30.6 are the owners of generic local–global compatibility and p-adic local Langlands. Existing upstream SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups owns the generic co-Whittaker API. The specific unconditional GL₂ family and essential-vector comparison of FW Props 6.7–6.9 still require the recorded supplier contract; the conditional general LLC-family node is not itself an unconditional proof.

nodes.title: The G_Σ-equivariant zeta morphism on completed homology
nodes.statement: For N ≥ 3, n ≥ 1 with prime(Np) = Σ and (n, Σ) = 1, Nakamura constructs from Kato's full-level Hecke-linear zeta classes a ℤ_p[GL_2(ℤ/N)]-linear map z^{Iw}_{N,n}(k, −): H¹(Y(N), 𝒱^*_k)(1) → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], H¹(X(N), j_*𝒱^*_k(2)))_{Q_{k,n}} (Prop. 3.8, Q_{k,n} the multiplicative set of the smoothing factors); after localizing at the non-Eisenstein ideal of ρ̄ it lands in the unlocalized Iwasawa cohomology of H¹(Y(N), 𝒱^*_k)_ρ̄(2) (Cor. 3.14, Prop. 3.15); the limits over p-power level define a continuous 𝕋_{ρ̄,Σ}[G_Σ]-linear map z^{Iw}_{Σ,n,ρ̄}: H̃^{BM}_{1,ρ̄,Σ} → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], H̃^{BM}_{1,ρ̄,Σ}(1)) with z(τv) = σ_{−1}z(v) and the Euler-system norm relations (Thm 3.16); and the weight-k maps are recovered from weight two by tensoring over O[[K_m]] with W = Sym^{k−2}(O²)^* (Prop. 3.17).
hypotheses: Localization at the non-Eisenstein maximal ideal of ρ̄ (absolutely irreducible) is what makes H¹(X(N), j_*𝒱) and H¹(Y(N), 𝒱) agree and the map integral.
proofSteps: Prop. 3.8: assemble Kato's classes c,d-z_{N,n}(k, r, r′) into a Hecke- and GL_2(ℤ/N)-equivariant map, removing the c,d smoothing in the localization Q_{k,n} (following Fukaya–Kato).

Use NAK-v2 Prop. 3.15 to remove the smoothing denominators after non-Eisenstein localization, via freeness and the finite-level comparison. Its c² smoothing coefficient is already correct in arXiv v2; PAPER-NAKAMURA-23/E5 concerns the later published bare-c misprint.
Thm 3.16: pass to the limit over N_0p^∞ and over levels in Σ_0; Prop. 3.17 compares weights.
acceptance: The modular input is imported from KatoEulerSystems:L2 (full-level Hecke-linear zeta classes), which says the universal-deformation map is owned here.

nodes.title: Nakamura's universal zeta morphism
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄: G_ℚ → GL_2(𝔽) satisfy (N1)–(N5) of L3/fw-residual-hypotheses (or (N1), (N3), (N4) with R_{ρ̄,Σ} replaced by the promodular ring 𝕋_{ρ̄,Σ}), with universal deformation ρ^u over R_{ρ̄,Σ}. There is a family of R_{ρ̄,Σ}-linear maps z_{Σ,n}(ρ^u): (ρ^u)^* → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σn, ζ_n], (ρ^u)^*(1)), n ≥ 1 prime to Σ, such that (i) z_{Σ,n}(ρ^u)(τv) = σ_{−1}z_{Σ,n}(ρ^u)(v) for complex conjugation τ; (ii) Cor ∘ z_{Σ,nl}(ρ^u) = z_{Σ,n}(ρ^u) if l | n and P_l(σ_l^{-1})·z_{Σ,n}(ρ^u) if (l, n) = 1; (iii) at every point x_f of Spec R_{ρ̄,Σ}(ℚ̄_p) attached to a newform f, z_{Σ,1}(f) = ∏_{l∈Σ∖{p}} P_{f,l}(σ_l^{-1})·z(f) with P_{f,l}(u) = det(1 − Frob_l u | ρ_f^{I_l}) (Nakamura Thm 1.1, Cor. 4.2, Thm 4.3). Condition (i) makes z_{Σ,n}(ρ^u) an R ⊗̂ Λ_n-linear map on (ρ^u)^* ⊗̂_{ℤ_p[±1]} Λ_n (Remark 1.2). It is defined by transporting z^{Iw}_{Σ,n,ρ̄} along φ_1 (L3/completed-homology-factorization), factoring out the projective envelope P̃ and applying the Whittaker functor Ψ_{Σ_0} at the primes of Σ_0 (§4.1, Lemma 4.1).
hypotheses: (N1)–(N5); FW's version (FW Thm 3.6) works under Assumptions 2.1 and 3.5 and removes p ≥ 5 via Paškūnas–Tung's generalization of the relevant local results (FW remark after Thm 3.6).
proofSteps: Lemma 4.1: φ_1 induces an isomorphism H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], H̃^{BM}_{1,ρ̄,Σ}(1)) ≅ (π^m_p)^* ⊗̂ H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], (ρ^m)^*(1) ⊗ B^m_{Σ_0}), via a perfect complex computing Iwasawa cohomology.

Remove the factor (π^m_p)^* using Paškūnas's identification of P̃ with the dual of the universal deformation of π̄ (removing-projective-envelope), and apply the Whittaker functor to B^m_{Σ_0}, which is co-Whittaker so that Ψ_{Σ_0}(B) ≅ 𝕋 (§4.1).
Properties (i)–(ii) follow from Thm 3.16 (Cor. 4.2); (iii) is L3/nakamura-specialization-theorem.
acceptance: It is the morphism FW call z_Σ: T_Σ(−1)^+ → H¹(ℤ[1/Σ], T_Σ) (FW Thm 3.6) after the identifications of FW §3.2.1.

nodes.title: The universal zeta morphism specializes to Kato's
nodes.statement: Under the assumptions of Nakamura §4 ((N1), (N3), (N4)), for every modular point x_f ∈ Spec(𝕋_{ρ̄,Σ})(E) attached to a newform f ∈ S_k(Γ_1(N_f))^{new} of weight k ≥ 2 and every n ≥ 1 prime to Σ, z_{Σ,n}(f) = ∏_{l∈Σ_0} P_{f,l}(σ_l^{-1})·z_n(f) as maps V′_1(f)_E → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σn, ζ_n], V′_1(f)_E(1)) under V′_1(f)_E ≅ ρ_f^* (55), where z_n(f) is Kato's (Nakamura-twisted) zeta morphism and Σ_0 = Σ ∖ {p}; the equality does not depend on the choice of (55) since End_{E[G_ℚ]}(ρ_f) = E (Nakamura Thm 4.3, Remark 4.4). In particular the morphism specializes to the Kato class used in KatoEulerSystems:L3–L4.
hypotheses: (N1), (N3), (N4); x_f modular.
proofSteps: Let τ be the Galois type of ρ_f|_{G_{ℚ_p}} and ⋄ = cr or st; x_f factors through Kisin's potentially semistable (crystalline) quotient R^⋄_p(k, τ) (Nakamura Thm 4.5).

Use NAK-v2 Cor. 4.8 and Prop. 4.9 with M^⋄(k,τ), the algebraic dual and σ^⋄(τ), tensoring over O[[K_0]] with completed BM homology. The type/coinvariant construction is essential and is not the plain tensor with W from a trivial local type.

Under these identifications z_{Σ,n}(f) is the base change of Ψ_{Σ_0}(z^{Iw}_{Σ_0,n,ρ̄}(k, σ^⋄(τ), −)); comparing motivic structures with Kato's construction (Nakamura §4.4, (68)–(78)) gives the equality with the Euler factors at Σ_0.
acceptance: The Euler factors at Σ_0 are exactly those of NakamuraZeta.classical; dropping them would contradict the change-of-Σ formula (79).

nodes.title: The zeta trivialization of the fundamental line
nodes.statement: Let z_Σ: T_Σ(−1)^+ → H¹_et(ℤ[1/Σ], T_Σ) be Nakamura's zeta morphism (FW Thm 3.6). Since H²_et(ℤ[1/Σ], T_Σ) is torsion and H¹ has generic rank equal to that of T_Σ(−1)^+ over 𝕋 (or over Λ), z_Σ determines an injective trivialization triv_{z_Σ}: Δ_Σ(T_Σ) ↪ Q(𝕋^Σ_{m_ρ̄}), equivalently an isomorphism Δ_Σ ≅ (x/y)𝕋 for an invertible fractional ideal (FW (1.2.1)); over Λ it gives triv_{z_Σ}: Δ_Σ(T_Σ) ↪ Frac Λ (Conj. 3.30's map). For every specialization λ: 𝕋 → R(𝔞) to a minimal prime and every classical point λ_f: R(𝔞) → O_Iw there are commutative diagrams relating triv_{z_Σ}, triv_{z(𝔞)} and triv_{z(f)_Iw} (FW (1.2.2), (1.2.3), Props 3.22–3.23), and for Iwasawa-suitable λ the same holds for the full fundamental lines with Euler factors. The Λ-valued map is obtained by the determinant after restriction of scalars; it is the norm construction, not an identification Q(T)=Frac Λ. Define the dual trivialization t^∨ on Δ_Σ^{-1}; if t^∨(Δ_Σ^{-1})=αΛ then t(Δ_Σ)=α^{-1}Λ. FW Prop. 5.5 proves integrality for this dual image.
hypotheses: FW Assumptions 2.1, 3.5; the specializations in the diagrams with full lines are Iwasawa-suitable (Def. 3.19).
proofSteps: Torsion of H² and the rank of H¹ over the total fraction ring (Kato's results at classical points, density) make Det^{-1}RΓ ⊗ Det^{-1}T(−1)^+ ⊗ Q(𝕋) canonically trivial once a generator of the image of z_Σ is chosen.
Compatibility with base change (L3/fundamental-line) and with specialization of z_Σ (L3/nakamura-specialization-theorem) gives the diagrams (FW Props 3.22–3.23).
Over Λ, view T_Σ as a free Λ-module of rank 2d and repeat (FW proof of Prop. 5.5).
acceptance: The universal main conjecture is the statement that the image of triv_{z_Σ} is 𝕋 (resp. Λ); over the non-factorial 𝕋 this cannot be deduced from pointwise statements, which is why the family statement is made over Λ.
