nodes.title: Kato's generalized main conjecture for the universal family and its specializations
nodes.statement: For an Iwasawa-suitable λ:T→S, FW Conj. 3.25 is the proposition that the Σ-partial zeta trivialization on the cyclotomic deformation T_{λ,Iw} has image S_Iw in Q(S_Iw). When S is a domain it also asserts the corresponding full-line trivialization Δ_{S_Iw}(T_{λ,Iw})≅S_Iw. The coefficient ring is S_Iw, not S. At a classical point Conj. 3.24 is the full O_Iw-line statement, equivalent to Kato’s characteristic-ideal equality. Conj. 3.27 states the minimal-component full-line assertion. Conj. 3.30 is the Σ-partial Λ-line statement for the regular subring Λ=O[[X_1,X_2,X_3]]; Conj. 3.26 is the separate stronger assertion over T itself.
hypotheses: The propositions are stated, not assumed; Λ-structure as in L3/universal-deformation-ring-structure.

Record the implications: Conj. 3.26 (over 𝕋) ⇒ Conj. 3.30 (over Λ) by restriction of scalars; Conj. 3.30 ⇒ Conj. 3.24 at classical points is FW Prop. 5.8 (L4/family-to-point-limit).
acceptance: Distinguishes the regular-subring statement of FW Thm 1.8 from the stronger statement over the deformation ring (stage L4's requirement).

nodes.title: The zeta trivialization over Λ is integral
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of FW Thm 5.1, let t_Λ:Δ_Σ(T_Σ)↪Frac Λ be the zeta trivialization and t_Λ^∨:Δ_Σ(T_Σ)^{-1}↪Frac Λ its dual. FW Prop. 5.5 gives t_Λ^∨(Δ_Σ^{-1})=αΛ with α∈Λ. Equivalently the primal image is α^{-1}Λ. This is an integrality bound on the dual lattice; equality with Λ still requires the seed-point argument.
hypotheses: FW Thm 5.1's residual hypotheses; Λ = O[[X_1, X_2, X_3]] factorial and regular.
The integral Kato bound needs its actual lattice/image hypotheses at the chosen classical points; this is part of kato-integral-quotient-witness, not supplied by residual irreducibility alone.
proofSteps: Suppose the image of Δ^{-1} is (x/y)Λ with x/y ∉ Λ; since Λ is factorial there is a height-one prime 𝔭 = (y_0) containing y but not x.

By density (L3/smooth-classical-points) choose an Iwasawa-suitable λ_Iw, étale over Λ, with λ(y_0) ∈ m^n_{O_Iw} and λ(x) ∉ m^n for large n; at such a point T_{λ,Iw} is a lattice in a direct sum of classical representations V_{λ,r,Iw}.

Kato's one-sided divisibility at each classical point (KatoEulerSystems:L4/cohomological-divisibility-one-direction, integral where T_{λ,Iw} has the needed image) gives t_Λ^∨(Δ^{-1}) ⊆ O_Iw at λ, contradicting λ(x/y) ∉ O_Iw.
acceptance: This uses only Kato's divisibility and density; Zariski density alone is not used to conclude that a rational section is an integral generator — the height-one prime argument over the factorial Λ is.

sources.match: The image of Δ_Σ(T_Σ)^{-1} lies in Λ, by a height-one prime of the factorial ring Λ and Kato's bound at well-chosen classical points.

nodes.title: From pointwise main conjectures at an étale point to the family over Λ
nodes.statement: Suppose there is a point x: Λ → O at which Spec 𝕋^Σ_{m_ρ̄} → Spec Λ is étale and every point ψ: 𝕋 → O above x satisfies Kato's main conjecture (FW Conj. 3.24). Then triv_{z_Σ}: Δ_Σ(T_Σ) ↪ Frac(Λ) is an isomorphism onto Λ (FW Prop. 5.7).
hypotheses: As stated; all λ_Iw above x are Iwasawa-suitable because of étaleness.
proofSteps: Use the dual trivialization of integrality-of-universal-trivialization, with image αΛ and α∈Λ.

Specialize along x_Iw: by the base-change diagram (FW Prop. 3.23; L3/zeta-trivialization), x_Iw(α)O_Iw is the product over ψ ∈ S_x of the pointwise images, each O_Iw by hypothesis, so x_Iw(α) is a unit.
An element of the local ring Λ whose specialization is a unit is a unit; hence αΛ = Λ.
acceptance: Every invertible module over the local deformation ring is abstractly free. The issue is the prescribed rational zeta trivialization: its lattice need not be the unit lattice. FW proves the needed integrality over the factorial regular subring Λ, then uses the finite étale fiber and its determinant norm to prove α is a unit.

nodes.title: Fouquet–Wan's universal-family main conjecture
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 3 and ρ̄: G_ℚ → GL_2(𝔽) satisfy the hypotheses of FW Thm 5.1 (absolutely irreducible; (ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}})^{ss} ≠ χ̄ ⊕ χ̄χ̄_cyc; a prime ℓ ∤ p with ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_ℓ}} a ramified extension of µχ^{−k/2}_cyc by µχ^{1−k/2}_cyc, µ unramified and nontrivial if ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is irreducible). For Σ finite, viewing the universal deformation T_Σ as a free module over Λ ≅ O[[X_1, X_2, X_3]], the zeta morphism z_Σ induces an isomorphism triv_{z_Σ}: Δ_Σ(T_Σ) ≅ Λ (FW Thm 5.2 = Thm 1.8; Kato's Conjecture 3.2.2 for (Spec ℤ[1/Σ], Λ, T_Σ)). The statement is over the regular subring Λ; the stronger statement over 𝕋 ≅ R_Σ(ρ̄) itself is not asserted.
hypotheses: FW Thm 5.1’s T51 residual hypotheses. For the even-weight Γ₀ modular normalization, the scalar local semisimplification is automatically excluded by the determinant parity argument of FW p. 69; see fw-pointwise-theorem.

The proof imports the ordinary/crystalline seed targets, whose general-weight nonvanishing, regulator and integral Kato-witness gaps remain explicit. No stronger theorem over the nonfactorial deformation ring is asserted.
proofSteps: Find a seed point: by FW Lemma 2.8 (L3/smooth-classical-points) there is a classical point that is crystalline-short, crystalline-short up to the quadratic twist ω^{(p−1)/2}, good ordinary, or good ordinary up to quadratic twist.

At such a point Kato's main conjecture holds (FW Prop. 5.6): crystalline-short points by L2/fw-crystalline-main-conjecture (Thm 4.51), ordinary points by the ordinary theorem — the ordinary seed is the equality of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1/fw-ordinary-theorem, which combines L2/fw-ordinary-reverse-bound with Kato's bound; twists are handled in the same way.
Points near the seed that are étale over Λ and of the same type satisfy the pointwise conjecture; apply L4/etale-point-descent.
acceptance: Exported to ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L4/fw-universal-family-theorem; the determinant over Λ must not be read as a statement over the deformation ring.

nodes.title: From the family over Λ to every classical point
nodes.statement: Assume the family Σ-partial trivialization is an isomorphism over Λ. FW Prop. 5.8 gives the corresponding Σ-partial trivialization at every classical point, including points ramified over Λ. Its morphism is the Euler-corrected z_Σ(f)_Iw. With the full-line local correction comparison of §§3.3–3.4 this yields Conj. 3.24 for the full line and Kato’s z(f)_Iw. Keep these two lines and their morphisms distinct; a specialized Euler factor that vanishes cannot simply be cancelled.
hypotheses: As stated; the Σ-partial lines and the Euler-factor-corrected morphisms are used, which both commute with specialization at a classical point even if it is ramified over Λ.
proofSteps: Kato’s bound puts the dual pointwise lattice in O_Iw, say γO_Iw with γ∈O_Iw. The primal lattice is then γ^{-1}O_Iw.
Over 𝕋 write the image of Δ_Σ as (α/β)𝕋 with λ(f)_Iw(β) ≠ 0 (FW Prop. 3.23).
Choose λ close to λ(f), outside the zero set of β, étale over Λ with all points above Iwasawa-suitable; the family isomorphism forces each pointwise γ_ψ to be a unit there, so λ_Iw(α/β) is a unit.
By continuity, taking λ close to λ(f), 1/γ = λ(f)_Iw(α/β) is a unit.
acceptance: A specialization at which a value vanishes is never cancelled: the argument avoids the zero set of β and works with the Euler-factor-corrected lines.

nodes.title: Fouquet–Wan's main conjecture at every point of the family
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 3 and f ∈ S_k(Γ_0(Np^r)) a normalized eigencuspform of weight k ≥ 2 whose residual representation satisfies the hypotheses of FW Thm 5.1 (L3/fw-residual-hypotheses, T51), with the auxiliary prime ℓ satisfying ℓ ∥ N. Then the zeta morphism gives an isomorphism triv_{z(f)_Iw}: Δ_{O_Iw}(T(f)_Iw) ≅ O_Iw (FW Thm 5.1; Thm 1.7 is its narrower nontrivial-µ formulation); equivalently char_{Λ_Iw}H²(ℤ[1/p], T ⊗ Λ_Iw) = char_{Λ_Iw}H¹(ℤ[1/p], T ⊗ Λ_Iw)/Λ_Iw·z(f)_Iw. This covers non-ordinary and bad-reduction points at p (π(f)_p principal series, Steinberg or supercuspidal) and needs no µ-invariant hypothesis. Consequences: Sel_ℚ(f) is finite iff L(f, k/2) ≠ 0 (Cor. 5.3), and for an abelian variety of GL_2-type with L(A,1) ≠ 0 satisfying the hypotheses, the p-part of the BSD formula holds (Cor. 5.4).
hypotheses: All hypotheses of FW Thm 5.1, including the global Γ₀ form, even k, and ℓ∥N. The Thm 1.7 formulation additionally requires µ nontrivial even in the reducible-at-p case.

The scalar local semisimplification is automatically impossible: det ρ̄_f|I_p=ω^{k−1} with k−1 odd; a scalar semisimplification would give ω^{2a} for some integer a, contradicting 2a≡k−1 mod p−1 because p is odd. Thus no additional scalar exclusion is missing from the displayed theorem (FW p. 69).

For the normalized residual representation in the proof on p. 73, the ramified Steinberg witness also excludes quadratic-induced restriction exceptions: its nontrivial unipotent p-element cannot occur in an induction from the index-two quadratic cyclotomic field, since ℓ≠p is unramified there and prime-to-p characters have no such inertia image. Together with the local exclusion, this supplies the A21/A35 dictionary; preserve the source’s critical twist.
proofSteps: Use the determinant-parity and Steinberg-witness arguments in the hypotheses to pass to the normalized residual datum of FW p. 73. The consumer’s alleged scalar-hypothesis source issue should be rejected, not propagated.
Apply L4/fw-universal-family-theorem to ρ̄_f.
Apply L4/family-to-point-limit at λ(f) (FW proof of Thm 5.1, p. 73).
Translate the fundamental-line statement into characteristic ideals over the regular O_Iw (L3/kato-generalized-main-conjecture, GenMC.point_iff_kato).
acceptance: Exported to ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L2/fw-pointwise-theorem in the cohomological (Kato) form; the signed or ordinary scalar versions are the consumer's, after its separate local comparison.

nodes.title: Euler factors, Tor terms and the regular subring in specialization
nodes.statement: For a specialization λ: A → A′ between quotients of 𝕋^Σ_{m_ρ̄} or Λ: (i) the Σ-partial fundamental line commutes with every base change, Δ_Σ(T) ⊗ A′ ≅ Δ_Σ(T′); (ii) the full fundamental line commutes with λ when λ is Iwasawa-suitable, the Euler-factor lines X_ℓ(T) specializing to X_ℓ(T′) because the ranks of inertia invariants and the eigenvalues α_ℓ are preserved (FW Prop. 3.20); otherwise the rank of T^{I_ℓ} can jump and the comparison acquires the factor relating X_ℓ(T) ⊗ A′ and X_ℓ(T′); (iii) Nakamura's change-of-Σ formula z_{Σ′,n} ⊗ id = ∏_{l∈Σ′∖Σ} P_l(σ_l^{-1})·z_{Σ,n} matches the passage from Δ_{Σ′} to Δ_Σ with the Euler factors P_l; (iv) a statement over the regular subring Λ (FW Thm 1.8) is a statement about T_Σ as a Λ-module of rank 2d, and at a point x of Λ it is a statement about the product over all points of 𝕋 above x — it implies the statement over 𝕋 only at points étale over Λ, and at ramified points only through L4/family-to-point-limit.
hypotheses: As stated; Iwasawa-suitable as in FW Def. 3.19.
proofSteps: (i)–(ii): perfectness and derived base change of RΓ (FW Lemma 3.17), and the explicit two-term complexes defining X_ℓ (FW Prop. 3.20's proof).
Use NAK-v2 change-of-Σ formula (77), p. 78, together with the H¹ isomorphism (78) and H² exact sequence (79), p. 80. These are different formulas and must not share a locator.
(iv): restriction of scalars along the finite free Λ → 𝕋 and the étale-point analysis of FW Props 5.7–5.8.
acceptance: A change of stable lattice is handled by the determinant of its global and local correction cones, with the specified Euler terms. It is not summarized by one unspecified scalar index. Use the universal lattice and record a full cone comparison before transporting a zeta basis.

nodes.title: Congruences between Kato's zeta morphisms
nodes.statement: Let f, g be normalized newforms with coefficients in E, ρ̄_f absolutely irreducible, and the assumptions of Nakamura §4 holding for ρ̄ = ρ̄_f. If f ≡ g modulo ϖ^m (Hecke eigenvalues congruent at all but finitely many primes), then ∏_{l∈Σ_0} P_{f,l}(σ_l^{-1})·z_n(f) ≡ ∏_{l∈Σ_0} P_{g,l}(σ_l^{-1})·z_n(g) modulo ϖ^m as maps ρ^*_{f,m} → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], ρ^*_{f,m}(1)) (Nakamura Cor. 5.6).
hypotheses: Nakamura §4 assumptions ((N1), (N3), (N4)); Σ containing the levels of f and g and p.
proofSteps: x_f and x_g are points of the same Spec 𝕋_{ρ̄,Σ} that agree modulo ϖ^m (the printed ϖ^n in the proof is ϖ^m, PAPER-NAKAMURA-23/E11).
Both Euler-corrected zeta morphisms are specializations of the one universal z_{Σ,n}(ρ^m) (L3/nakamura-specialization-theorem), so they agree modulo ϖ^m.
acceptance: This is the congruence of zeta morphisms that propagates Kato's main conjecture along congruences (L4/nakamura-lambda-defect).

nodes.title: The residual zeta morphism and the space of points X(ρ̄)
nodes.statement: Let Σ_ρ̄ = {p} ∪ ram(ρ̄). For Σ_ρ̄ ⊆ Σ ⊆ Σ′, ρ^m_{Σ′} ⊗ 𝕋_{ρ̄,Σ} ≅ ρ^m_Σ and z_{Σ′,n}(ρ^m_{Σ′}) ⊗ id = ∏_{l∈Σ′∖Σ} P_l(σ_l^{-1})·z_{Σ,n}(ρ^m_Σ) (Nakamura (77)). The residual zeta morphism z_{Σ,n}(ρ̄) is the base change of z_{Σ,n}(ρ^m) to 𝔽, a Λ_{n,𝔽}-linear map ρ̄^* ⊗_{𝔽[±1]} Λ_{n,𝔽} → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σn, ζ_n], ρ̄^*(1)). Put X(ρ̄) = ∪_Σ Spec(𝕋_{ρ̄,Σ})(ℤ̄_p) with its modular points X(ρ̄)^{mod}, and for a character η of Δ = Gal(ℚ(ζ_p)/ℚ) consider η-components over Λ^η.
hypotheses: Nakamura §4 assumptions; absolute irreducibility of ρ̄.
proofSteps: Base change of z_{Σ,n}(ρ^m) along 𝕋_{ρ̄,Σ} → 𝔽, using that H¹_Iw is computed by a perfect complex.
Compatibility with change of Σ from (77).

nodes.title: Residual nonvanishing, µ = 0 and the structure of residual Iwasawa cohomology
nodes.statement: Fix a character η of Δ. (i) The following are equivalent: z_{Σ_ρ̄,1}(ρ̄)^η ≠ 0; µ(H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_f], ρ_f^*(1))^η/Im(z_1(f)^η)) = 0 for some x_f ∈ X(ρ̄)^{mod}; the same for all x_f ∈ X(ρ̄)^{mod} (Nakamura Thm 5.7; the published version adds Conj. 5.8 that these always hold). (ii) Assume X(ρ̄)^{mod}_a ≠ ∅ (modular points with Nakamura's condition (a)) and (i) holds for η. Then H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_ρ̄], ρ̄^*(1))^η is free of rank one over Λ^η_𝔽, and H¹_Iw/Im(z_{Σ_ρ̄,1}(ρ̄)^η) and H²_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_ρ̄], ρ̄^*(1))^η are finite-dimensional (arXiv Thm 5.8 = published Thm 5.9); the η-part of Kato's main conjecture for ρ̄ is the equality of their dimensions (arXiv Conj. 5.9 = published 5.10). (iii) For every x ∈ Spec(𝕋_{ρ̄,Σ})(O) ⊂ X(ρ̄): H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ], ρ_x^*(1))^η is free of rank one over Λ^η_O; the quotient by Im z_{Σ,1}(ρ_x)^η and H²_Iw are torsion with µ = 0; and if x is modular, or there is τ ∈ Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ(ζ_{p^∞})) with (ρ_x/(τ−1)ρ_x)[1/p] one-dimensional, then Char(H¹_Iw/Im z^η) ⊆ Char(H²_Iw^η) (arXiv Thm 5.10 = published Thm 5.11).
hypotheses: Nakamura §4 assumptions. In (ii)–(iii), assume both residual nonvanishing in the selected η-component and existence of a modular point satisfying condition (a) of NAK-v2 Thm 5.2: there is τ∈Gal(Q̄/Q(ζ_p∞)) such that ρ_f/(τ−1)ρ_f is O-free of rank one. A quotient of rational dimension one alone does not meet this integral condition.

Under these inputs, rank-one freeness, torsion and µ=0 hold at all promodular points. The characteristic-ideal containment in (iii) additionally needs modularity or the weaker rational condition (b); do not infer it at every promodular point.
proofSteps: (i): the mod-ϖ exact sequences relating H¹_Iw(ρ_f^*(1))/ϖ and H¹_Iw(ρ̄^*(1)), freeness of H¹_Iw (Kato Thm 12.4(3)) and L4/zeta-morphism-congruences.
(ii): Kato's theorem 5.2 at a point of X^{mod}_a gives the rank and finiteness; descend modulo ϖ.

(iii): lift freeness and torsion from the residual statement; µ = 0 from (i); the divisibility from the Euler system bound (EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems:ES.8 / KatoEulerSystems:L4) under the image condition.
acceptance: Residual nonvanishing and the integral condition-(a) modular witness are hypotheses. The theorem does not prove unconditional µ=0. The published additional conjecture of nonvanishing is absent from arXiv v2.

nodes.title: The λ-defect is constant on the family and Kato's main conjecture propagates along congruences
nodes.statement: Under the assumptions of L4/nakamura-residual-structure (ii), for every x ∈ X(ρ̄): λ(H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ], ρ_x^*(1))^η/Im z_{Σ,1}(ρ_x)^η) − λ(H²_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ], ρ_x^*(1))^η) equals dim_𝔽(H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_ρ̄], ρ̄^*(1))^η/Im z_{Σ_ρ̄,1}(ρ̄)^η) − dim_𝔽 H²_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_ρ̄], ρ̄^*(1))^η, hence is independent of x (arXiv Thm 5.13 = published Thm 5.14); consequently the η-part of Kato's main conjecture for ρ̄ holds iff the weak (λ-) version holds for some x iff it holds for all x (arXiv Cor. 5.14 = published Cor. 5.15). In particular (Nakamura Thm 1.4): if g_1, g_2, g_3 are congruent to f with (1) some τ ∈ Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ(ζ_{p^∞})) making ρ_{g_1}/(τ − 1)ρ_{g_1} free of rank one over O, (2) µ = 0 for g_2, and (3) Kato's main conjecture for g_3, then µ = 0 and Kato's main conjecture hold for f.
hypotheses: As in L4/nakamura-residual-structure; the proof's last display prints H¹ for H² (PAPER-NAKAMURA-23/E12, corrected).
proofSteps: For a module with µ = 0, λ(M) = λ_𝔽(M/ϖ) − λ_𝔽(M[ϖ]) (Nakamura (92)); apply it to H¹_Iw/Im z and to H²_Iw and use the residual comparison (91).

Constancy gives the equivalence of weak λ-equality at some/all promodular points and the residual equality. Full characteristic-ideal equality additionally uses the one-sided containment, available for modular points or those satisfying condition (b) of Thm 5.2; it is not asserted at every promodular point merely from equal λ-invariants.
Thm 1.4 is the specialization of these statements to modular points, as in Kim–Lee–Ponsinet.
acceptance: Gives the pointwise consequences of the universal zeta element that stage L4 owns (Nakamura §5); the conjectures are recorded as propositions, not assumed.

The scalar ordinary main conjecture with canonical periods, the curve-to-form lattice and Manin-constant transport and the final assembly are ModularIwasawaMainConjectures L1–L3's, which import the endpoints directly from L5b and L4.

nodes.title: Interface: the ordinary two-variable Perrin-Riou/Greenberg equivalence (BCS Theorem 4.1.3, Corollary 4.1.4)
nodes.statement: Let g ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) be an elliptic newform, p ∤ 2N an ordinary prime for g, and K imaginary quadratic with p split (spl), (D_K, N) = 1 and ρ̄_g irreducible over G_K (irr_K). The following are equivalent: (i) X_ord(g/K_∞) is Λ_K-torsion and (L^{PR}_p(g/K)) ⊇ ch_{Λ_K}(X_ord(g/K_∞)) in Λ_K ⊗ ℚ_p; (ii) X_Gr(g/K_∞) is Λ_K-torsion and (L^{Gr}_p(g/K)) ⊇ ch_{Λ_K}(X_Gr(g/K_∞)) in Λ^{ur}_K ⊗ ℚ_p; the same holds for the opposite divisibilities and before inverting p (BCS Thm 4.1.3, from BSTW §9.3.2). For two newforms g, g′ with p ∤ 2NN′ ordinary for both and K satisfying (spl), (D_K, NN′) = 1 and (irr_K) for both, the product statements (L^{PR}_p(g/K)·L^{PR}_p(g′/K)) ⊇ ch(X_ord(g/K_∞))·ch(X_ord(g′/K_∞)) and (L^{Gr}_p(g/K)·L^{Gr}_p(g′/K)) ⊇ ch(X_Gr(g/K_∞))·ch(X_Gr(g′/K_∞)) are equivalent, in either direction (BCS Cor. 4.1.4). This node states the exact contract L5a consumes; its proof (the ordinary BSTW two-variable zeta element, both explicit reciprocity laws, and the two four-term Poitou–Tate sequences) belongs to the planned owner KatoEulerSystems L5 of RS-11, which does not yet exist.
hypotheses: BCS Thm 4.1.3 has (irr_K), which implies H⁰(K,g[p])=0 and hence the van_K condition needed in the integral comparison. The source asserts both directions, including the integral version under these hypotheses. No claim is made about what survives if van_K is removed outside this setting.
BCS cite the theorem as Proposition 4.1.3 in the proof of Prop. 5.2.1; it is Thm 4.1.3 in v2 (RT-AREA-iwasawa-1/29).
proofSteps: Writing H for the rank-one global module, Z for the two-variable zeta class and X_st for the strict Selmer dual, the two Poitou–Tate sequences give ch(H/ΛZ)·ch(X_Gr) = (L_Gr)·ch(X_st) and ch(H/ΛZ)·ch(X_ord) = (L_PR)·ch(X_st) after the unramified coefficient extension, using both explicit reciprocity laws (RS-11 handoff).
Prove rank one, torsion and nonvanishing of the terms before cancelling; this gives ch(X_Gr)·(L_PR) = ch(X_ord)·(L_Gr), hence both directions of the equivalence.
Cor. 4.1.4: direct sums of the two pairs of sequences for g and g′.
acceptance: Does not use the anticyclotomic Theorem 4.2.1, which belongs to HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.8/HE.8b.

nodes.title: Restricting the quartic-CM characteristic ideal to K
nodes.statement: Let g ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) be an elliptic newform, p > 3 a good ordinary prime with ρ̄_g irreducible, F a real quadratic field, K imaginary quadratic, M = FK the quartic CM field, K̃_∞ = FK_∞, Λ̃_K = O[[Gal(K̃_∞/M)]] ≅ Λ_K and π_K: Λ_M → Λ̃_K ≅ Λ_K induced by Gal(M_∞/M) ↠ Gal(K̃_∞/M). Then π_K(ch_{Λ_M}(X_ord(g/M_∞))) ⊇ ch_{Λ_K}(X_ord(g/K_∞))·ch_{Λ_K}(X_ord(g^F/K_∞)) in Λ_K, where g^F is the twist of g by the quadratic character of F/ℚ (BCS Lemma 5.1.1).
hypotheses: As in BCS §5; the containment is integral and in the stated direction only.
proofSteps: Use control at I_K to identify the restricted quartic Selmer module with the corresponding module over M with coefficients T_g⊗Λ̃_K^∨. Shapiro then identifies it with the direct sum of the two Selmer modules over K for T_g and T_g⊗η_F; the right-hand cohomology groups are over K, not M as printed in BCS p. 9. The quadratic character η_F is trivial on G_M.
Restriction from M to K of a module induced along Gal(M/K) ≅ Gal(F/ℚ) splits by the characters of Gal(M/K) (Shapiro).
SU Cor. 3.8 (journal): π_K(ch_{Λ_M}(X)) ⊇ ch_{Λ_K}(X/I_K) (L0/selmer-specialization-control (ii)).
acceptance: Direction check: the image of the quartic characteristic ideal contains the product of the two K-characteristic ideals, so a divisibility for M gives one for the product over K.

nodes.title: The quartic-CM p-adic L-function restricted to K
nodes.statement: In the setting of L5a/quartic-cm-selmer-restriction, (π_K(L_p(g^F/M))) = (L^{PR}_p(g/K)·L^{PR}_p(g^F/K)) in Λ_K ⊗ ℚ_p, where L_p(g^F/M) is Wan's p-adic L-function of the base change g_F over M (BCS Lemma 5.1.2).
hypotheses: The identity is only after inverting p (the comparison of interpolation properties involves periods whose p-integral comparison is open — BCS Remark 1.1.3(ii)).
proofSteps: Compare interpolation formulas on a Zariski-dense set of characters of Γ_K: the base-change L-value L(g_F/M ⊗ χ, 1) factors as L(g/K ⊗ χ, 1)·L(g^F/K ⊗ χ, 1) (Wan's Prop. 84 in the journal numbering).

The interpolation comparison identifies the restricted function with the product up to the fixed nonzero period scalar and the specified normalizations. After inverting p this scalar is a unit, giving equality of principal ideals. Density alone cannot remove the period scalar to yield an exact identity of normalized functions.

nodes.title: Existence of the auxiliary fields K and F
nodes.statement: Let g ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) be an elliptic newform and p ≥ 5 a prime of good ordinary reduction with ρ̄_g irreducible over G_ℚ. There exist an imaginary quadratic K satisfying (disc) (D_K odd, D_K ≠ −3), (Heeg) (every ℓ | N splits in K), (spl) (p splits in K) and (irr_K), and a real quadratic F with (i) p inert in F, (ii) D_F odd with every prime dividing D_F split in K, (iii) every ℓ | N inert in F if ℓ ≡ −1 mod p and split otherwise, (iv) (irr_M) for M = FK, (v) ρ̄_g|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} irreducible, (vi) F ≠ ℚ(ζ_5)^+ if p = 5 (BCS Lemma 5.2.3). Moreover such M/F satisfies (pN, D_F) = 1, (N O_F, D_{M/F}) = 1, (spl_F) and (Δ), and n^- = O_F, so the hypotheses of Wan's theorem (L5w) other than Hypothesis 3.1.1 hold, and (H1)–(H3) follow from (v), (vi), the minimal-lift argument and (iii) (proof of BCS Prop. 5.2.1).
hypotheses: As stated; the conditions are independent splitting conditions satisfied by a positive proportion of quadratic fields.
proofSteps: Since p ∤ N, conditions (i) and (iii) on F are independent splitting conditions; fix F with odd D_F.
Similarly (spl), (Heeg) and (ii) hold for a positive proportion of K; choose one with (disc) and (irr_K).

(irr_M) holds if FK is not in the splitting field of ρ_g|_{G_K}; if ρ̄_g|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} is reducible, ρ̄_g|_{G_F} is induced from an index-two subgroup containing G_{F(ζ_p)}, which forces p = 5 and F = ℚ(ζ_5)^+.

Check the hypotheses of BCS Thm 3.2.1: (ii) gives n^- = O_F; (H2) from the base change of a minimal modular lift (Wan's Thm 103); (H3) from (iii) (AutomorphicCongruences:L5w/selected-base-change-hypotheses).
acceptance: Answers the L5b request for Lemma 5.2.3; the stronger 'new ramified K-prime outside D_F' requirement mentioned there is not in BCS v2 and is not added.
HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.8b/auxiliary-quadratic-field-verification consumes this node (HE.8b comes after L5a); it is not a prerequisite here.

The splitting tests include the prime 2 when 2 divides N. For an odd fundamental discriminant D, 2 splits when D≡1 (mod 8) and is inert when D≡5 (mod 8). The Jacobi-symbol criterion is used only at odd primes. The suggested integer predicates distinguish these cases.

nodes.title: Vanishing of the µ-invariant of the Greenberg function
nodes.statement: Let g ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) be an elliptic newform with good reduction at p > 2 and K satisfying (disc), (Heeg), (spl) and (irr_K). Then µ(L^{Gr}_p(g/K)) = µ(L^{BDP}_p(g/K)) = 0 (BCS Prop. 4.2.2). Here L_p^{BDP} is BCS §2’s normalized BDP function, which already interpolates the squared quantity. The comparison of principal ideals in Prop. 4.2.2 introduces no additional square.
hypotheses: As stated; the projection comparison is CGS23 Prop. 1.4.5 (Lemma 2.4.4/Prop. 2.4.5 in a later version), which needs Rubin's main conjecture and the Hida–Tilouine input for the CM factor.

The projection of L^{Gr}_p(g/K) to Λ^{-,ur}_K generates the same ideal as L^{BDP}_p(g/K) by comparing interpolation properties (CGS23 Prop. 1.4.5); µ of a two-variable function is bounded by µ of a one-variable specialization.

nodes.statement: Let g ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) be an elliptic newform, p ≥ 5 a good ordinary prime, K satisfying (disc), (Heeg), (spl), (irr_K), and F a real quadratic field satisfying (i)–(vi) of L5a/auxiliary-field-existence. µ(L^{Gr}_p(g/K)·L^{Gr}_p(g^F/K)) = 0 (L5a/greenberg-mu-vanishing for g and g^F), so the Greenberg containment holds integrally in Λ^{ur}_K; Cor. 4.1.4 again gives the integral Perrin-Riou containment.

conventions.selmer: Σ relaxes conditions away from p only. The chosen Greenberg condition at every v|p remains in force even when v∈Σ. Characteristic divisors use height-one lengths over noetherian normal domains for finite torsion modules; ideal containments there mean the associated divisorial fractional ideals. Native principal characteristic ideals are used only when factoriality is available.
conventions.divisibility: 'Ch ⊆ (L)' (equivalently L divides Ch) is the reverse divisibility proved by Eisenstein congruences; Kato's Euler-system bound is the opposite one.
conventions.periods: SU's p-adic L-functions use the canonical periods Ω^±_f; no comparison with Gross periods is assumed.
conventions.frobenius: Use each source’s stated Frobenius and reciprocity convention. SU Lemma 3.2.17 specifically uses P_T,ℓ(X)=det(1−X frob_ℓ^{-1};(T⊗Frac A)^{I_ℓ}) and substitutes ℓ^{-1}ε(frob_ℓ). Nakamura’s newform polynomial is 1−a_ℓX+ℓ^{k−1}ε(ℓ)X². Transport duals, twists and inverse Frobenius explicitly.
conventions.quadraticSplitting: For fundamental discriminants D, the Jacobi criterion at an odd prime applies when the prime is unramified. At 2 and odd D, splitting means D≡1 mod 8 and inertia means D≡5 mod 8. Include this distinction when 2 divides a level.
